exercises.description: Stand tall with an even foundation and relaxed shoulders. This quiet pose builds postural awareness and steady attention.
steps: Bring your feet together and spread your weight evenly across both soles.
Engage your legs and lengthen through the crown of your head.
Rest your arms beside you with palms forward and chin level.
Breathe evenly, letting your chest rise without lifting your shoulders.
exercises.breath: Inhale grow tall · exhale soften shoulders
exercises.cue: Root through both feet; rise through your crown.
exercises.tip: Stand with your feet hip-width apart if bringing them together feels unsteady.
exercises.watch: Watch how the weight spreads evenly through both feet, the legs wake up, and the crown of the head rises while the shoulders stay soft.
exercises.name: Mountain Pose

exercises.description: An overhead reach turns a grounded stance into a full-body stretch. Build shoulder awareness while keeping your ribs balanced over your pelvis.
steps: Stand with your feet together and your weight evenly distributed.
Inhale, reach both arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Keep your arms shoulder-width apart and soften your lower ribs.
Breathe steadily, reaching through your fingertips with your gaze slightly lifted.
exercises.cue: Reach upward without pushing your ribs forward.
exercises.tip: Keep your arms wider apart or lower them slightly if your shoulders feel restricted.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms reach straight up from the shoulders while the ribs stay soft and the feet stay rooted.
exercises.name: Upward Salute

exercises.description: Fold from your hips and let your head hang toward the mat. This standing stretch develops hamstring flexibility and awareness of your back body.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and soften your knees.
Exhale, hinge at your hips and fold your torso over your thighs.
Touch your fingertips beside your feet and release your neck.
Inhale to lengthen your spine; exhale to settle into the fold.
exercises.cue: Bend your knees enough to free your spine.
exercises.tip: Rest your hands on blocks and bend your knees more to keep the fold comfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the fold come from the hips, not the waist. The knees stay soft, so the spine can hang long and the neck can relax.
exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold

exercises.description: Lengthen your torso forward into a flat-backed hinge. This active pause builds back strength and clarity in hip-hinging movements.
steps: Start in a standing fold with your feet hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips on your shins and inhale your chest forward.
Straighten your legs and lengthen your back parallel to the floor.
Keep your neck aligned with your spine and breathe into your ribs.
exercises.cue: Reach your chest forward, not your chin.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees slightly and place your hands higher on your shins to find a long spine.
exercises.watch: Watch the back become long and flat, like a tabletop, with the fingertips on the shins and the gaze just ahead of the feet.
exercises.name: Halfway Lift

exercises.description: Sit your hips back while reaching your arms overhead. Chair builds leg strength and core endurance through a grounded, active hold.
steps: Stand with your feet together and press through your heels.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back, keeping your spine long.
Reach your arms alongside your ears as your torso leans slightly forward.
Inhale through your fingertips; exhale to sit a little deeper without losing length.
exercises.cue: Send your hips back while lifting your chest.
exercises.tip: Use a shallower knee bend and keep your hands on your hips.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips sit back as if into a chair, the weight in the heels, and the arms reaching long beside the ears.
exercises.name: Chair Pose

exercises.description: A grounded back heel anchors this upright lunge. Build leg strength and shoulder reach while exploring the relationship between your hips and feet.
steps: Step one foot back, turning its toes outward about forty-five degrees; ground the heel.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and keep your back leg strong.
Turn your hips toward the front and raise your arms overhead, palms facing.
Inhale to reach taller; exhale to settle into your front leg.
exercises.cue: Ground your back heel as your arms rise.
exercises.tip: Widen your stance side to side and bend your front knee less to make turning forward easier.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee bend over the ankle while the back heel stays grounded and the hips face forward, then the arms rise.
exercises.name: Warrior I · Right

exercises.description: A grounded back heel anchors this upright lunge. Build leg strength and shoulder reach while exploring the relationship between your hips and feet.
steps: Step one foot back, turning its toes outward about forty-five degrees; ground the heel.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and keep your back leg strong.
Turn your hips toward the front and raise your arms overhead, palms facing.
Inhale to reach taller; exhale to settle into your front leg.
exercises.cue: Ground your back heel as your arms rise.
exercises.tip: Widen your stance side to side and bend your front knee less to make turning forward easier.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee bend over the ankle while the back heel stays grounded and the hips face forward, then the arms rise.
exercises.name: Warrior I · Left

exercises.description: Open your stance and reach through both arms above strong legs. Warrior II builds lower-body endurance and steady, purposeful focus.
steps: Step your feet wide; turn your front toes out and back toes slightly inward.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and keep your back leg straight.
Extend your arms at shoulder height, palms down, with your torso centered over your hips.
Look beyond your front fingertips and breathe, reaching equally through both hands.
exercises.cue: Track your front knee in line with your toes.
exercises.tip: Shorten your stance and reduce the front knee bend while keeping both feet grounded.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee stay right over the ankle, the torso stay upright between the legs, and the arms reach long in both directions.
exercises.name: Warrior II · Right

exercises.description: Open your stance and reach through both arms above strong legs. Warrior II builds lower-body endurance and steady, purposeful focus.
steps: Step your feet wide; turn your front toes out and back toes slightly inward.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and keep your back leg straight.
Extend your arms at shoulder height, palms down, with your torso centered over your hips.
Look beyond your front fingertips and breathe, reaching equally through both hands.
exercises.cue: Track your front knee in line with your toes.
exercises.tip: Shorten your stance and reduce the front knee bend while keeping both feet grounded.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee stay right over the ankle, the torso stay upright between the legs, and the arms reach long in both directions.
exercises.name: Warrior II · Left

exercises.description: Keep your lunge grounded as your upper body arcs toward the back leg. This standing reach builds leg endurance and length through your side body.
steps: Take a wide stance with your front knee bent and back leg straight.
Rest your back hand lightly on your back thigh.
Sweep your front arm overhead and arc your torso toward your back leg.
Inhale into your extended side, keeping your front knee bent and gaze lifted.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee bent as you reach back.
exercises.tip: Keep your overhead arm lower and look forward rather than up.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs stay exactly as in Warrior Two while the front arm sweeps up and back and the back hand rests lightly on the leg.
exercises.name: Reverse Warrior · Right

exercises.description: Keep your lunge grounded as your upper body arcs toward the back leg. This standing reach builds leg endurance and length through your side body.
steps: Take a wide stance with your front knee bent and back leg straight.
Rest your back hand lightly on your back thigh.
Sweep your front arm overhead and arc your torso toward your back leg.
Inhale into your extended side, keeping your front knee bent and gaze lifted.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee bent as you reach back.
exercises.tip: Keep your overhead arm lower and look forward rather than up.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs stay exactly as in Warrior Two while the front arm sweeps up and back and the back hand rests lightly on the leg.
exercises.name: Reverse Warrior · Left

exercises.description: A forearm-supported lunge creates a long diagonal from heel to fingertips. Build leg endurance while exploring space through your ribs and chest.
steps: Step your feet wide, turn your front toes out, and bend your front knee over your ankle.
Rest your front forearm on your front thigh without collapsing your shoulder.
Reach your top arm over your ear and turn your chest open.
Inhale along your top side; exhale to stay grounded through both feet, gazing upward.
exercises.cue: Lengthen from your back heel to your top fingertips.
exercises.tip: Keep your top hand on your hip and look down to simplify the balance.
exercises.watch: Watch one long diagonal line from the back heel to the top fingertips, with the forearm resting on the thigh and the chest turning open.
exercises.name: Extended Side Angle · Right

exercises.description: A forearm-supported lunge creates a long diagonal from heel to fingertips. Build leg endurance while exploring space through your ribs and chest.
steps: Step your feet wide, turn your front toes out, and bend your front knee over your ankle.
Rest your front forearm on your front thigh without collapsing your shoulder.
Reach your top arm over your ear and turn your chest open.
Inhale along your top side; exhale to stay grounded through both feet, gazing upward.
exercises.cue: Lengthen from your back heel to your top fingertips.
exercises.tip: Keep your top hand on your hip and look down to simplify the balance.
exercises.watch: Watch one long diagonal line from the back heel to the top fingertips, with the forearm resting on the thigh and the chest turning open.
exercises.name: Extended Side Angle · Left

exercises.description: Reach sideways over a straight front leg and open your chest. Triangle develops hamstring flexibility and awareness of length through both sides of your waist.
steps: Step your feet wide, turning your front toes out and back toes slightly inward.
Keep both legs straight and reach your torso sideways over your front leg.
Rest your bottom hand on your shin and extend your top arm toward the ceiling.
Inhale to lengthen your waist; exhale to open your chest, looking toward your top hand.
exercises.cue: Lengthen both sides of your waist.
exercises.tip: Place your bottom hand on a block, soften your front knee, and look down.
exercises.watch: Watch both legs stay straight while the body lengthens sideways over the front leg, then the top arm lifts in line with the bottom one.
exercises.name: Triangle Pose · Right

exercises.description: Reach sideways over a straight front leg and open your chest. Triangle develops hamstring flexibility and awareness of length through both sides of your waist.
steps: Step your feet wide, turning your front toes out and back toes slightly inward.
Keep both legs straight and reach your torso sideways over your front leg.
Rest your bottom hand on your shin and extend your top arm toward the ceiling.
Inhale to lengthen your waist; exhale to open your chest, looking toward your top hand.
exercises.cue: Lengthen both sides of your waist.
exercises.tip: Place your bottom hand on a block, soften your front knee, and look down.
exercises.watch: Watch both legs stay straight while the body lengthens sideways over the front leg, then the top arm lifts in line with the bottom one.
exercises.name: Triangle Pose · Left

exercises.description: A wide squat pairs strong legs with an upright spine and open arms. Build lower-body endurance while coordinating your knees and feet.
steps: Stand wide with your toes turned outward.
Bend your knees in line with your toes and lower your hips.
Lift your arms into a cactus shape, elbows bent and palms forward.
Inhale to grow tall; exhale to sit lower while keeping your knees tracking over your toes.
exercises.cue: Keep your knees moving in the direction of your toes.
exercises.tip: Use a smaller knee bend and rest your hands on your hips.
exercises.watch: Watch the feet turn out wide, the knees bend in the same direction as the toes, and the spine stay tall between them.
exercises.name: Goddess Pose

exercises.description: Fold between widely spaced feet with strong legs and a released neck. This shape develops hamstring flexibility and a clear sense of grounding.
steps: Step your feet wide and keep them parallel.
Exhale, hinge at your hips and lower your torso between your legs.
Place your palms on the mat between your feet, keeping your legs engaged.
Breathe steadily and release your crown toward the mat without forcing depth.
exercises.cue: Keep your weight balanced across both feet.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees and place your hands on blocks to give your spine more room.
exercises.watch: Watch the feet step wide and parallel, the legs stay strong, and the body fold from the hips with the hands under the shoulders.
exercises.name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold

exercises.description: Fold over your front leg while keeping both feet grounded. Pyramid develops hamstring flexibility and balance within a compact standing stance.
steps: Step one foot back about a leg's length and ground both heels.
Turn your hips toward your front foot and lengthen both legs.
Hinge forward over your front leg, placing fingertips beside your front foot.
Inhale to extend your spine; exhale to fold without rounding your shoulders.
exercises.cue: Lengthen forward before folding farther.
exercises.tip: Place your hands on blocks and soften your front knee to keep your back long.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips square to the front, the spine lengthen forward first, and only then fold over the front leg.
exercises.name: Pyramid Pose · Right

exercises.description: Fold over your front leg while keeping both feet grounded. Pyramid develops hamstring flexibility and balance within a compact standing stance.
steps: Step one foot back about a leg's length and ground both heels.
Turn your hips toward your front foot and lengthen both legs.
Hinge forward over your front leg, placing fingertips beside your front foot.
Inhale to extend your spine; exhale to fold without rounding your shoulders.
exercises.cue: Lengthen forward before folding farther.
exercises.tip: Place your hands on blocks and soften your front knee to keep your back long.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips square to the front, the spine lengthen forward first, and only then fold over the front leg.
exercises.name: Pyramid Pose · Left

exercises.description: Rise above a long, heel-lifted lunge with your arms overhead. Build leg strength and balance while reaching in opposite directions.
steps: Step one foot back onto the ball of your foot.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and straighten your back leg.
Bring your torso upright, square your hips forward, and reach both arms overhead.
Inhale through your fingertips; exhale to steady your hips above your strong legs.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee stacked over your ankle.
exercises.tip: Lower your back knee to the mat and place your hands on your front thigh.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee stack over the ankle, the back heel lift, and the back leg stay straight and strong as the arms reach up.
exercises.name: High Crescent Lunge · Right

exercises.description: Rise above a long, heel-lifted lunge with your arms overhead. Build leg strength and balance while reaching in opposite directions.
steps: Step one foot back onto the ball of your foot.
Bend your front knee over your ankle and straighten your back leg.
Bring your torso upright, square your hips forward, and reach both arms overhead.
Inhale through your fingertips; exhale to steady your hips above your strong legs.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee stacked over your ankle.
exercises.tip: Lower your back knee to the mat and place your hands on your front thigh.
exercises.watch: Watch the front knee stack over the ankle, the back heel lift, and the back leg stay straight and strong as the arms reach up.
exercises.name: High Crescent Lunge · Left

exercises.description: Settle into a wide, upright squat with your palms together. Garland explores hip and ankle mobility while building awareness of a long spine.
steps: Stand slightly wider than your hips with your toes turned outward.
Bend your knees and lower your hips between your heels.
Bring your palms together at your chest and press your elbows lightly against your inner knees.
Inhale to lift your spine; exhale to settle your hips with your heels grounded.
exercises.cue: Lift your chest without forcing your knees outward.
exercises.tip: Sit on a block or place a folded blanket under your heels if they lift.
exercises.watch: Watch the heels root down, the hips sink low between them, and the elbows gently press the knees open as the chest lifts.
exercises.name: Garland Pose

exercises.description: Add a chest-opening twist to a grounded chair shape. This pose combines leg endurance with rotational control and focused balance.
steps: Stand with your feet together, bend your knees, and sit your hips back.
Bring your palms together at your chest and lengthen your spine.
Rotate your torso and hook the opposite elbow outside your outer knee, keeping both knees level.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale to rotate your chest without shifting your knees.
exercises.cue: Keep your knees level as your chest turns.
exercises.tip: Practice a shallow chair with hands at your heart, adding a small twist without hooking your elbow.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees stay level in Chair Pose while the chest turns and the elbow hooks outside the opposite knee.
exercises.name: Revolved Chair · Right

exercises.description: Add a chest-opening twist to a grounded chair shape. This pose combines leg endurance with rotational control and focused balance.
steps: Stand with your feet together, bend your knees, and sit your hips back.
Bring your palms together at your chest and lengthen your spine.
Rotate your torso and hook the opposite elbow outside your outer knee, keeping both knees level.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale to rotate your chest without shifting your knees.
exercises.cue: Keep your knees level as your chest turns.
exercises.tip: Practice a shallow chair with hands at your heart, adding a small twist without hooking your elbow.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees stay level in Chair Pose while the chest turns and the elbow hooks outside the opposite knee.
exercises.name: Revolved Chair · Left

exercises.description: Reach overhead and arc sideways from a steady standing base. Build side-body length and awareness of how your ribs move with breath.
steps: Stand with your feet together and weight even.
Reach both arms overhead and bring your palms together.
Shift your hips slightly opposite your bend and arc your body sideways.
Inhale to lengthen upward; exhale into the curve while keeping your chest facing forward.
exercises.cue: Create length through your top side, not a forward fold.
exercises.tip: Separate your feet hip-width and keep your hands on your hips for a smaller side bend.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms join overhead and the body curve sideways like a crescent moon, without leaning forward.
exercises.name: Standing Side Bend · Right

exercises.description: Reach overhead and arc sideways from a steady standing base. Build side-body length and awareness of how your ribs move with breath.
steps: Stand with your feet together and weight even.
Reach both arms overhead and bring your palms together.
Shift your hips slightly opposite your bend and arc your body sideways.
Inhale to lengthen upward; exhale into the curve while keeping your chest facing forward.
exercises.cue: Create length through your top side, not a forward fold.
exercises.tip: Separate your feet hip-width and keep your hands on your hips for a smaller side bend.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms join overhead and the body curve sideways like a crescent moon, without leaning forward.
exercises.name: Standing Side Bend · Left

exercises.description: Balance on one leg with your lifted knee opening outward. Tree builds standing stability and steady attention through a simple, upright shape.
steps: Stand tall and transfer your weight into your standing foot.
Open your lifted knee outward and place its sole against your inner standing thigh, above the knee.
Press your palms together at your chest and level your hips.
Fix your gaze on one still point and breathe evenly through small balance adjustments.
exercises.cue: Press foot and inner thigh toward each other.
exercises.tip: Use a wall and place your lifted foot against your inner calf, avoiding the knee joint.
exercises.watch: Watch the standing foot root down, the other foot press into the inner thigh or calf, never the knee, and the gaze rest on one point.
exercises.name: Tree Pose · Right

exercises.description: Balance on one leg with your lifted knee opening outward. Tree builds standing stability and steady attention through a simple, upright shape.
steps: Stand tall and transfer your weight into your standing foot.
Open your lifted knee outward and place its sole against your inner standing thigh, above the knee.
Press your palms together at your chest and level your hips.
Fix your gaze on one still point and breathe evenly through small balance adjustments.
exercises.cue: Press foot and inner thigh toward each other.
exercises.tip: Use a wall and place your lifted foot against your inner calf, avoiding the knee joint.
exercises.watch: Watch the standing foot root down, the other foot press into the inner thigh or calf, never the knee, and the gaze rest on one point.
exercises.name: Tree Pose · Left

exercises.description: Balance in a long line from fingertips to lifted heel. This forward-reaching shape builds standing-leg strength and control through your core.
steps: Shift your weight into one foot and soften your standing knee.
Hinge forward, extending your lifted leg back until your torso and leg approach parallel with the floor.
Reach both arms forward alongside your ears; flex your lifted foot and keep your hips level.
Breathe steadily, reaching forward through your hands and back through your heel.
exercises.cue: Keep both hip points facing the mat.
exercises.tip: Rest your hands on a chair and keep your lifted leg lower.
exercises.watch: Watch the body tip forward as one long line from the hands to the lifted heel, with both hip points facing the floor.
exercises.name: Warrior III · Right

exercises.description: Balance in a long line from fingertips to lifted heel. This forward-reaching shape builds standing-leg strength and control through your core.
steps: Shift your weight into one foot and soften your standing knee.
Hinge forward, extending your lifted leg back until your torso and leg approach parallel with the floor.
Reach both arms forward alongside your ears; flex your lifted foot and keep your hips level.
Breathe steadily, reaching forward through your hands and back through your heel.
exercises.cue: Keep both hip points facing the mat.
exercises.tip: Rest your hands on a chair and keep your lifted leg lower.
exercises.watch: Watch the body tip forward as one long line from the hands to the lifted heel, with both hip points facing the floor.
exercises.name: Warrior III · Left

exercises.description: Wrap your arms and legs into a compact standing balance. Eagle builds leg endurance and concentration while stretching across your upper back.
steps: Bend both knees and shift your weight into your standing leg.
Cross your lifted thigh over your standing thigh and hook your lifted foot behind your calf.
Cross your standing-leg-side arm underneath the other, wrap your forearms, and bring your palms together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height; breathe steadily as you sit your hips back.
exercises.cue: Sit back while keeping your gaze steady.
exercises.tip: Rest your lifted toes on the floor like a kickstand and hold opposite shoulders instead of wrapping your arms.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees bend first, then the legs and arms wrap, while the hips sit back and the gaze stays steady.
exercises.name: Eagle Pose · Right

exercises.description: Wrap your arms and legs into a compact standing balance. Eagle builds leg endurance and concentration while stretching across your upper back.
steps: Bend both knees and shift your weight into your standing leg.
Cross your lifted thigh over your standing thigh and hook your lifted foot behind your calf.
Cross your standing-leg-side arm underneath the other, wrap your forearms, and bring your palms together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height; breathe steadily as you sit your hips back.
exercises.cue: Sit back while keeping your gaze steady.
exercises.tip: Rest your lifted toes on the floor like a kickstand and hold opposite shoulders instead of wrapping your arms.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees bend first, then the legs and arms wrap, while the hips sit back and the gaze stays steady.
exercises.name: Eagle Pose · Left

exercises.description: Kick your lifted foot into your hand as your chest reaches forward. Dancer combines standing balance with an active stretch across the chest and front thigh.
steps: Stand on one leg and bend your lifted knee behind you.
Hold the inside of your lifted foot with the hand on that same side.
Kick your foot back and up, tip your torso forward, and reach your free arm diagonally forward.
Inhale to broaden your chest; exhale to steady your standing foot and keep your gaze focused.
exercises.cue: Kick into your hand rather than pulling your foot.
exercises.tip: Hold a wall with your free hand and keep your lifted thigh low.
exercises.watch: Watch the hand hold the back foot, then the foot kicks into the hand to lift the leg, while the front arm reaches forward.
exercises.name: Dancer Pose · Right

exercises.description: Kick your lifted foot into your hand as your chest reaches forward. Dancer combines standing balance with an active stretch across the chest and front thigh.
steps: Stand on one leg and bend your lifted knee behind you.
Hold the inside of your lifted foot with the hand on that same side.
Kick your foot back and up, tip your torso forward, and reach your free arm diagonally forward.
Inhale to broaden your chest; exhale to steady your standing foot and keep your gaze focused.
exercises.cue: Kick into your hand rather than pulling your foot.
exercises.tip: Hold a wall with your free hand and keep your lifted thigh low.
exercises.watch: Watch the hand hold the back foot, then the foot kicks into the hand to lift the leg, while the front arm reaches forward.
exercises.name: Dancer Pose · Left

exercises.description: Balance on one leg while opening your chest and hips sideways. Half Moon builds standing stability and coordination through an expansive, reaching shape.
steps: Shift onto your standing foot and place your fingertips on the mat ahead of it.
Lift your other leg straight behind you until it is parallel to the floor.
Stack your hips open and extend your top arm toward the ceiling, keeping your standing leg strong.
Breathe steadily and lengthen through your lifted heel as your chest opens.
exercises.cue: Lift your bottom waist instead of sinking into your hand.
exercises.tip: Place your bottom hand on a block and rest your back against a wall for support.
exercises.watch: Watch the weight shift onto one leg and one hand, the top hip stack over the bottom hip, and the chest turn open to the side.
exercises.name: Half Moon · Right

exercises.description: Balance on one leg while opening your chest and hips sideways. Half Moon builds standing stability and coordination through an expansive, reaching shape.
steps: Shift onto your standing foot and place your fingertips on the mat ahead of it.
Lift your other leg straight behind you until it is parallel to the floor.
Stack your hips open and extend your top arm toward the ceiling, keeping your standing leg strong.
Breathe steadily and lengthen through your lifted heel as your chest opens.
exercises.cue: Lift your bottom waist instead of sinking into your hand.
exercises.tip: Place your bottom hand on a block and rest your back against a wall for support.
exercises.watch: Watch the weight shift onto one leg and one hand, the top hip stack over the bottom hip, and the chest turn open to the side.
exercises.name: Half Moon · Left

exercises.description: Balance your knees on your upper arms with both feet lifted. Crow develops arm strength, core engagement, and patient control of your weight shift.
steps: Squat and place your palms shoulder-width apart with fingers spread.
Bend your elbows and bring your knees high onto the backs of your upper arms.
Shift your chest forward, look ahead on the mat, and lift your feet with big toes touching.
Press the floor away and breathe evenly while drawing your heels toward your seat.
exercises.cue: Look forward and shift gradually, rather than jumping.
exercises.tip: Keep your toes grounded while practicing the forward weight shift, then lift one foot at a time.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees settle high on the upper arms, the gaze move forward, and the weight shift slowly into the hands until the feet float.
exercises.name: Crow Pose

exercises.description: Hold a long line from head to heels on straight arms. High Plank builds coordinated strength through your core, shoulders, and legs.
steps: Place your hands beneath your shoulders with fingers spread.
Step your feet back, tuck your toes, and straighten your legs.
Align your head, hips, and heels while pressing the floor away.
Look down slightly ahead of your hands and breathe steadily into your ribs.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips in line with your shoulders and heels.
exercises.tip: Lower both knees to the mat while keeping a straight line from your head to your knees.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands under the shoulders and the body form one straight line from head to heels, with the belly gently drawn in.
exercises.name: High Plank

exercises.description: Lower your knees, chest, and chin while keeping your hips lifted. This low shape develops arm control and awareness through a small backbend.
steps: Start on hands and knees with your toes tucked.
Bend your elbows close to your ribs and shift your chest forward and down.
Rest your chest and chin on the mat, keeping your hips lifted and palms beside your chest.
Breathe evenly, keeping your elbows pointing back and avoiding pressure through your neck.
exercises.cue: Let your chest share the contact, not just your chin.
exercises.tip: Skip the chin contact and lower onto your belly, resting your forehead on the mat instead.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees lower first, then the chest and chin come down between the hands while the hips stay lifted.
exercises.name: Knees-Chest-Chin

exercises.description: Hover in a low plank with your elbows close to your ribs. This demanding hold builds arm strength and precise whole-body control.
steps: Begin in high plank with your hands beneath your shoulders.
Shift forward onto your toes and bend your elbows close to your ribs.
Lower until your shoulders reach elbow height, keeping your forearms vertical and body in one line.
Breathe steadily, pressing through your palms without letting your chest drop lower.
exercises.breath: Inhale prepare · exhale lower with control
exercises.cue: Keep your shoulders no lower than your elbows.
exercises.tip: Lower your knees first, then bend your elbows through a small range while keeping your chest supported.
exercises.watch: Watch the body lower as one straight line, elbows hugging the ribs, stopping when the shoulders are level with the elbows.
exercises.name: Low Plank

exercises.description: Lift your chest just above the mat with elbows bent. Low Cobra builds back strength while inviting a broad chest and a long neck.
steps: Lie on your belly with legs extended and the tops of your feet grounded.
Place your palms under your shoulders and tuck your elbows close to your ribs.
Inhale, lift your chest slightly while keeping your elbows bent and shoulders drawn back and down.
Exhale to lower slightly, keeping your neck long and gaze forward and down.
exercises.cue: Lift through your back rather than pushing your arms straight.
exercises.tip: Keep your chest closer to the mat and reduce pressure through your hands.
exercises.watch: Watch the chest lift with the strength of the back, the elbows stay bent, and the hips and legs stay on the mat.
exercises.name: Cobra Pose

exercises.description: Press through your hands and the tops of your feet to lift your chest and thighs. This active backbend builds arm strength and expands your front body.
steps: Lie on your belly with your palms beside your lower ribs and legs extended.
Press into your hands and the tops of your feet to straighten your arms.
Lift your hips and thighs off the mat, bringing your shoulders over your wrists.
Inhale to broaden your chest forward; exhale to steady your strong legs with your gaze forward.
exercises.cue: Keep your thighs lifted and shoulders away from your ears.
exercises.tip: Choose Low Cobra with your thighs grounded and elbows bent instead.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms straighten, the chest open forward, and the thighs lift off the mat while the shoulders move away from the ears.
exercises.name: Upward-Facing Dog

exercises.description: Lift your hips into an inverted V with hands and feet grounded. Build shoulder strength while lengthening through your back body.
steps: Start on hands and knees with palms shoulder-width apart and fingers spread.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back, straightening your arms and legs.
Lengthen your spine and release your head between your upper arms.
Inhale to lift your hips; exhale to reach your heels toward the mat.
exercises.cue: Prioritize a long spine over heels touching the mat.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees generously and let your heels lift to keep your spine long.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips lift up and back into an upside-down V. The spine stays long first, and the heels reach toward the mat second.
exercises.name: Downward-Facing Dog

exercises.description: Extend one leg from Downward-Facing Dog without tipping your pelvis. This reaching balance develops shoulder stability and control through your hips and core.
steps: Begin in Downward-Facing Dog with your palms spread and spine long.
Lift one leg straight up and back in line with your torso.
Flex your lifted foot and keep both hip points facing the mat.
Inhale to reach through your lifted heel; exhale to balance weight evenly between your hands.
exercises.breath: Inhale reach heel · exhale level hips
exercises.cue: Keep your hips level rather than lifting your leg higher.
exercises.tip: Keep your lifted leg lower or rest its toes on the floor behind you.
exercises.watch: Watch the leg lift straight back from Downward Dog while both hips stay level, rather than kicking the leg as high as possible.
exercises.name: Three-Legged Dog · Right

exercises.description: Extend one leg from Downward-Facing Dog without tipping your pelvis. This reaching balance develops shoulder stability and control through your hips and core.
steps: Begin in Downward-Facing Dog with your palms spread and spine long.
Lift one leg straight up and back in line with your torso.
Flex your lifted foot and keep both hip points facing the mat.
Inhale to reach through your lifted heel; exhale to balance weight evenly between your hands.
exercises.breath: Inhale reach heel · exhale level hips
exercises.cue: Keep your hips level rather than lifting your leg higher.
exercises.tip: Keep your lifted leg lower or rest its toes on the floor behind you.
exercises.watch: Watch the leg lift straight back from Downward Dog while both hips stay level, rather than kicking the leg as high as possible.
exercises.name: Three-Legged Dog · Left

exercises.description: Ground your back knee and lift your arms above an upright lunge. This pose develops hip-flexor length and a steady, supported standing-leg foundation.
steps: Step one foot forward between your hands and lower your back knee.
Rest your back foot on the mat; stack your front knee over your ankle.
Lift your torso upright and reach both arms overhead.
Inhale to lengthen upward; exhale to let your hips move slightly forward without arching your lower back.
exercises.cue: Lift your torso as your hips settle forward.
exercises.tip: Pad your back knee with a folded blanket and keep your hands on your front thigh.
exercises.watch: Watch the back knee rest on the mat, the hips sink forward, and the chest lift as the arms reach up.
exercises.name: Low Lunge · Right

exercises.description: Ground your back knee and lift your arms above an upright lunge. This pose develops hip-flexor length and a steady, supported standing-leg foundation.
steps: Step one foot forward between your hands and lower your back knee.
Rest your back foot on the mat; stack your front knee over your ankle.
Lift your torso upright and reach both arms overhead.
Inhale to lengthen upward; exhale to let your hips move slightly forward without arching your lower back.
exercises.cue: Lift your torso as your hips settle forward.
exercises.tip: Pad your back knee with a folded blanket and keep your hands on your front thigh.
exercises.watch: Watch the back knee rest on the mat, the hips sink forward, and the chest lift as the arms reach up.
exercises.name: Low Lunge · Left

exercises.description: Link a standing reach and forward fold in one flowing breath cycle. This simple sequence builds breath coordination and fluid movement through your spine and shoulders.
steps: Stand with your feet together and arms beside you.
Inhale, sweep both arms out and overhead.
Exhale, fold from your hips with soft knees and reach your hands toward the mat.
Inhale, rise all the way to standing, sweeping your arms overhead.
Exhale, lower your arms beside you and return to your tall starting stance.
exercises.breath: Inhale rise · exhale fold or lower
exercises.cue: Let each breath guide the pace of your movement.
exercises.tip: Stand with feet hip-width apart and make the fold shallow, keeping your knees bent.
exercises.watch: Watch how every movement rides on the breath: arms rise as she breathes in, and fold down as she breathes out.
exercises.name: Sun Breath Flow

exercises.description: Shift between an inverted V and a long, straight plank. These waves build shoulder and core endurance while coordinating movement with breath.
steps: Begin in Downward-Facing Dog with your hips high and palms firmly grounded.
Inhale, shift forward until your shoulders stack over your wrists in high plank.
Pause briefly with your head, hips, and heels aligned, pressing the floor away.
Exhale, press your hips up and back into Downward-Facing Dog; repeat with your breath.
exercises.breath: Inhale shift forward · exhale press back
exercises.cue: Move your whole body together rather than dropping your hips.
exercises.tip: Lower your knees during the plank phase, then lift them as you press back into Downward-Facing Dog.
exercises.watch: Watch the whole body move together, rolling forward from Downward Dog into Plank and back again, without the hips dropping.
exercises.name: Down Dog to Plank Waves

exercises.description: Alternate a lifted chest and rounded back on hands and knees. This flowing sequence develops spinal awareness and a clear connection between breath and movement.
steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders, knees under hips, and back flat.
Inhale, lower your belly and lift your chest and tailbone, looking forward.
Exhale, round your spine upward and tuck your chin and tailbone.
Return to a flat tabletop, then repeat the cycle at the pace of your breath.
exercises.cue: Spread the movement along your spine without forcing your neck.
exercises.tip: Keep the movements small and place a folded blanket under your knees.
exercises.watch: Watch the movement start at the tailbone and travel up the spine: the belly drops and the chest opens, then the back rounds like a cat.
exercises.name: Cat–Cow

exercises.description: Support a long, steady body line on parallel forearms. This grounded hold builds core endurance and shoulder stability.
steps: Place your forearms parallel on the mat with elbows beneath your shoulders.
Step your feet back and tuck your toes, lifting your knees.
Align your head, hips, and heels while pressing firmly through your forearms.
Look down and breathe into your ribs, keeping your hips steady.
exercises.cue: Press your forearms down without letting your hips sag.
exercises.tip: Keep both knees on the mat and maintain a straight line from your head to your knees.
exercises.watch: Watch the elbows sit under the shoulders and the body hold one straight line, with the hips neither lifted nor sagging.
exercises.name: Forearm Plank

exercises.description: Balance sideways on one hand and stacked feet. Side Plank builds side-body strength and shoulder stability through a lifted, expansive line.
steps: Begin in high plank and shift your weight into your supporting hand.
Turn onto the outer edge of your bottom foot and stack your feet and legs.
Lift your hips and reach your top arm up, hand under shoulder.
Look forward and breathe evenly, maintaining a long line from head to heels.
exercises.cue: Press the floor away and keep your bottom waist lifted.
exercises.tip: Lower your bottom knee to the mat and extend your top leg for a supported side plank.
exercises.watch: Watch the body turn onto one hand and the side of the foot, the hips lift high, and the top arm reach to the sky.
exercises.name: Side Plank · Right

exercises.description: Balance sideways on one hand and stacked feet. Side Plank builds side-body strength and shoulder stability through a lifted, expansive line.
steps: Begin in high plank and shift your weight into your supporting hand.
Turn onto the outer edge of your bottom foot and stack your feet and legs.
Lift your hips and reach your top arm up, hand under shoulder.
Look forward and breathe evenly, maintaining a long line from head to heels.
exercises.cue: Press the floor away and keep your bottom waist lifted.
exercises.tip: Lower your bottom knee to the mat and extend your top leg for a supported side plank.
exercises.watch: Watch the body turn onto one hand and the side of the foot, the hips lift high, and the top arm reach to the sky.
exercises.name: Side Plank · Left

exercises.description: Balance with a lifted chest, bent knees, and shins parallel to the floor. Boat builds core endurance and hip-flexor strength without needing straight legs.
steps: Sit with your knees bent and feet on the mat.
Lean back slightly with a long spine and lift your feet, keeping your knees bent.
Bring your shins parallel to the floor and reach your arms forward alongside your knees.
Inhale to lift your chest; exhale to steady your balance on your sitting bones.
exercises.cue: Lift your chest rather than rounding your back.
exercises.tip: Hold behind your thighs or keep your toes lightly grounded while maintaining a lifted chest.
exercises.watch: Watch the chest stay lifted and the back stay long as the feet float up, knees bent first, legs straighter only if the back stays long.
exercises.name: Boat Pose

exercises.description: Lift your hips above a firm forearm foundation. Dolphin builds shoulder strength while exploring length through your spine and hamstrings.
steps: Place parallel forearms on the mat with elbows beneath your shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your knees, sending your hips up and back.
Keep your head free between your upper arms and press your forearms down.
Inhale to lift your hips; exhale to lengthen your spine with strong, steady shoulders.
exercises.cue: Press through your forearms so your shoulders stay lifted.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees and keep your heels lifted to reduce the stretch behind your legs.
exercises.watch: Watch the forearms press down and the hips lift high, like Downward Dog on the elbows, with the head hanging free.
exercises.name: Dolphin Pose

exercises.description: Reach opposite limbs away from a steady tabletop base. Bird Dog develops core coordination and balance while keeping your spine long.
steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward at shoulder height and the opposite leg back at hip height.
Keep your back flat, hips level, and gaze down.
Breathe evenly, reaching through your lifted fingertips and back heel without shifting your torso.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips level as your limbs reach away.
exercises.tip: Keep your reaching fingertips or extended toes on the mat, or practice extending one limb at a time.
exercises.watch: Watch the opposite arm and leg reach away at the same time, while the hips stay level and the back stays still.
exercises.name: Bird Dog · Right

exercises.description: Reach opposite limbs away from a steady tabletop base. Bird Dog develops core coordination and balance while keeping your spine long.
steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward at shoulder height and the opposite leg back at hip height.
Keep your back flat, hips level, and gaze down.
Breathe evenly, reaching through your lifted fingertips and back heel without shifting your torso.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips level as your limbs reach away.
exercises.tip: Keep your reaching fingertips or extended toes on the mat, or practice extending one limb at a time.
exercises.watch: Watch the opposite arm and leg reach away at the same time, while the hips stay level and the back stays still.
exercises.name: Bird Dog · Left

exercises.description: Alternate opposite arm and leg reaches while lying on your back. This controlled sequence builds core coordination and awareness of your pelvis and spine.
steps: Lie on your back; reach your arms upward and bend your knees over your hips, shins parallel.
Exhale, lower one arm overhead and extend the opposite leg low, keeping your lower back grounded.
Inhale, return your arm and leg to the starting position.
Repeat with the other arm and leg, exhaling to extend and inhaling to return.
exercises.cue: Shorten your reach if your lower back starts to lift.
exercises.tip: Keep your arms still and tap one bent-leg heel toward the mat at a time.
exercises.watch: Watch the lower back stay heavy on the mat while the opposite arm and leg lower slowly toward the floor and return.
exercises.name: Dead Bug

exercises.description: Lift your pelvis from a grounded base of feet, arms, and shoulders. Bridge builds glute strength and invites space across your chest.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart near your hips.
Rest your arms beside you and press your feet into the mat.
Lift your hips into a slope from knees to shoulders, keeping your knees aligned over your feet.
Inhale to broaden your chest; exhale to steady with space under your chin.
exercises.cue: Press evenly through both feet and keep your neck still.
exercises.tip: Lift your hips only a little and keep your arms firmly grounded.
exercises.watch: Watch the feet press evenly into the mat and the hips rise one vertebra at a time, while the head and neck stay still.
exercises.name: Bridge Pose

exercises.description: Lift your chest, arms, and legs from your belly. This active backbend strengthens your back body and develops awareness of a long, open posture.
steps: Lie on your belly with legs together and arms beside you, palms facing down.
Reach your fingertips back and lengthen through your toes.
Inhale, lift your chest, arms, and straight legs slightly off the mat.
Keep your neck long and gaze down and forward as you breathe steadily.
exercises.cue: Reach long rather than lifting as high as possible.
exercises.tip: Keep your feet grounded and lift only your chest a small amount.
exercises.watch: Watch the chest, arms and legs lift together off the mat, reaching long rather than high, with the neck in line.
exercises.name: Locust Pose

exercises.description: Rest on your forearms with your chest lifted in a low backbend. Sphinx develops awareness of spinal extension and space across the front of your chest.
steps: Lie on your belly with your legs extended behind you.
Place your elbows under your shoulders and keep your forearms parallel.
Press your forearms down to lift your chest, letting your shoulders settle away from your ears.
Look forward and breathe slowly into your belly without forcing the arch.
exercises.cue: Lift your chest without compressing your lower back.
exercises.tip: Slide your elbows farther forward to lower your chest and reduce the backbend.
exercises.watch: Watch the elbows settle under the shoulders and the chest rise gently, keeping the lower back soft and the face relaxed.
exercises.name: Sphinx Pose

exercises.description: Arch your chest upward from a kneeling base, reaching back to your heels. Camel develops front-body length and controlled spinal extension.
steps: Kneel with your knees hip-width apart and the tops of your feet on the mat.
Place your hands on your pelvis and lift your chest as your hips stay over your knees.
Arch through your upper back and reach your hands to your heels without dropping your hips backward.
Inhale to lift your chest; breathe steadily, letting your head tip back only as your neck allows.
exercises.breath: Inhale lift chest · exhale stay grounded
exercises.cue: Keep your hips above your knees and lift your chest.
exercises.tip: Keep your hands on your pelvis and practice a small chest lift without reaching for your heels.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips stay over the knees, the chest lift up first, and only then the hands reach back toward the heels.
exercises.name: Camel Pose

exercises.description: Hold your ankles and kick back to lift your chest and thighs. Bow builds back-body strength and length across your chest and front thighs.
steps: Lie on your belly, bend both knees, and reach your hands back.
Hold the outsides of your ankles and keep your knees roughly hip-width apart.
Kick your feet back into your hands to lift your chest and thighs, gazing forward.
Inhale to lift slightly; exhale to steady, allowing only a small natural rock with your breath.
exercises.cue: Kick back into your hands instead of pulling your ankles.
exercises.tip: Practice Locust with your feet grounded and chest slightly lifted before adding the ankle hold.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands hold the ankles, then the feet kick back into the hands so the chest and thighs lift together.
exercises.name: Bow Pose

exercises.description: Press through hands and feet into a full-body arch. Wheel demands coordinated arm and leg strength while developing shoulder mobility and front-body length.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Place your palms beside your head with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through hands and feet to lift, keeping your neck relaxed.
Breathe evenly, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking in line with your toes.
exercises.cue: Share the lift between your hands and feet.
exercises.tip: Practice Bridge instead, keeping your arms and shoulders grounded while building a steady lift through your hips.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands set beside the ears, the hips rise first, then the arms straighten, sharing the lift between hands and feet.
exercises.name: Wheel Pose

exercises.description: Lift your chest on a forearm foundation with your legs extended. This version of Fish explores chest opening and controlled upper-back extension without added props.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs extended and arms close to your body.
Press your forearms into the mat and lift your chest toward the ceiling.
Keep your weight in your forearms as you lightly rest your crown on the mat.
Inhale to lift your chest; exhale to soften your throat without loading your head.
exercises.breath: Inhale lift chest · exhale soften throat
exercises.cue: Support the lift through your forearms, not your head.
exercises.tip: Keep your head supported on a folded blanket and make the chest lift smaller if crown contact strains your neck.
exercises.watch: Watch the forearms take the weight under the body, the chest lift, and the head rest lightly without carrying any load.
exercises.name: Supported Fish

exercises.description: Walk your hands forward from kneeling while keeping your hips above your knees. Puppy develops shoulder mobility and length through your chest and spine.
steps: Start on hands and knees with your knees beneath your hips.
Walk your hands forward, stretching your arms long with palms grounded.
Keep your hips over your knees and lower your forehead toward the mat.
Exhale to let your chest descend; inhale along your spine without forcing your shoulders.
exercises.cue: Keep your hips stacked above your knees.
exercises.tip: Rest your forehead on a block or folded blanket and keep your chest higher.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips stay right over the knees while the hands walk forward and the chest melts toward the mat.
exercises.name: Extended Puppy

exercises.description: A low, wide lunge explores hip extension while building steady support through your hands and front foot.
steps: Begin on hands and knees; step one foot outside the hand on that side.
Lower your back knee and place both hands inside your front foot.
Lengthen your chest forward, keeping your front knee aligned with your toes.
Breathe slowly, allowing your hips to settle slightly on each exhale.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee tracking with your toes.
exercises.tip: Place a folded blanket under your back knee and keep your hips higher.
exercises.watch: Watch the front foot step outside the hand, the front knee track with the toes, and the hips settle low and forward.
exercises.name: Lizard Pose · Right

exercises.description: A low, wide lunge explores hip extension while building steady support through your hands and front foot.
steps: Begin on hands and knees; step one foot outside the hand on that side.
Lower your back knee and place both hands inside your front foot.
Lengthen your chest forward, keeping your front knee aligned with your toes.
Breathe slowly, allowing your hips to settle slightly on each exhale.
exercises.cue: Keep your front knee tracking with your toes.
exercises.tip: Place a folded blanket under your back knee and keep your hips higher.
exercises.watch: Watch the front foot step outside the hand, the front knee track with the toes, and the hips settle low and forward.
exercises.name: Lizard Pose · Left

exercises.description: This upright hip stretch pairs a folded front leg with a long back leg, developing hip mobility and a composed seat.
steps: Begin on hands and knees; bring one knee forward behind the hand on that side.
Angle your front shin across the mat and extend your other leg straight back.
Rest fingertips beside your hips and lengthen your spine, keeping your pelvis facing forward.
Inhale to grow taller; exhale to settle without forcing your front knee.
exercises.cue: Keep the front knee free of strain.
exercises.tip: Support your front hip with a folded blanket, or choose reclined figure four if your knee feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the front shin settle across the mat, the back leg stretch long behind, and the hips stay level before folding forward.
exercises.name: Half Pigeon · Right

exercises.description: This upright hip stretch pairs a folded front leg with a long back leg, developing hip mobility and a composed seat.
steps: Begin on hands and knees; bring one knee forward behind the hand on that side.
Angle your front shin across the mat and extend your other leg straight back.
Rest fingertips beside your hips and lengthen your spine, keeping your pelvis facing forward.
Inhale to grow taller; exhale to settle without forcing your front knee.
exercises.cue: Keep the front knee free of strain.
exercises.tip: Support your front hip with a folded blanket, or choose reclined figure four if your knee feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the front shin settle across the mat, the back leg stretch long behind, and the hips stay level before folding forward.
exercises.name: Half Pigeon · Left

exercises.description: Bound Angle brings the soles together in an upright seat, building postural awareness while stretching the inner thighs.
steps: Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together near your pelvis.
Open your knees outward and hold your feet gently.
Lift through your spine without pulling your feet or pressing your knees.
Breathe evenly, letting your knees soften downward on each exhale.
exercises.cue: Lift your spine; let your knees soften.
exercises.tip: Sit on a folded blanket and support your thighs with cushions.
exercises.watch: Watch the soles of the feet come together, the knees open wide, and the spine lift tall instead of pushing the knees down.
exercises.name: Bound Angle

exercises.description: A playful reclined hip stretch invites easy movement while building awareness of your back and pelvis.
steps: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest.
Open your knees toward your armpits and hold the outer edges of your feet.
Face your soles upward, keeping your shins vertical and your head and sacrum resting down.
Breathe slowly and rock gently from side to side.
exercises.cue: Keep your head and sacrum resting down.
exercises.tip: Hold behind your thighs instead of reaching for your feet.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees open beside the ribs, the hands hold the feet, and the head and lower back stay resting on the mat.
exercises.name: Happy Baby

exercises.description: This reclined hip stretch targets the outer hip while keeping your head and shoulders supported.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, above the knee, and flex the crossed foot.
Lift the supporting foot and clasp your hands behind that thigh.
Exhale to draw your legs closer while keeping your head and shoulders relaxed.
exercises.cue: Flex the crossed foot; relax your shoulders.
exercises.tip: Keep the supporting foot on the floor and rest your head on a folded blanket.
exercises.watch: Watch one ankle cross over the opposite knee, the foot stay flexed, and the hands gently draw the legs closer while the shoulders rest.
exercises.name: Reclined Figure Four · Right

exercises.description: This reclined hip stretch targets the outer hip while keeping your head and shoulders supported.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, above the knee, and flex the crossed foot.
Lift the supporting foot and clasp your hands behind that thigh.
Exhale to draw your legs closer while keeping your head and shoulders relaxed.
exercises.cue: Flex the crossed foot; relax your shoulders.
exercises.tip: Keep the supporting foot on the floor and rest your head on a folded blanket.
exercises.watch: Watch one ankle cross over the opposite knee, the foot stay flexed, and the hands gently draw the legs closer while the shoulders rest.
exercises.name: Reclined Figure Four · Left

exercises.description: A kneeling hamstring stretch develops a long spine and awareness of the back of your extended leg.
steps: Begin in a low lunge with your back knee down.
Shift your hips over your back knee and straighten your front leg, heel grounded and toes lifted.
Place fingertips beside your front leg and hinge forward with a long spine.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale into a modest fold.
exercises.cue: Lead with your chest, not your chin.
exercises.tip: Bend your front knee slightly and place a folded blanket under your back knee.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips move back over the back knee, the front leg straighten with the toes lifted, and the chest lengthen forward.
exercises.name: Half Split · Right

exercises.description: A kneeling hamstring stretch develops a long spine and awareness of the back of your extended leg.
steps: Begin in a low lunge with your back knee down.
Shift your hips over your back knee and straighten your front leg, heel grounded and toes lifted.
Place fingertips beside your front leg and hinge forward with a long spine.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale into a modest fold.
exercises.cue: Lead with your chest, not your chin.
exercises.tip: Bend your front knee slightly and place a folded blanket under your back knee.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips move back over the back knee, the front leg straighten with the toes lifted, and the chest lengthen forward.
exercises.name: Half Split · Left

exercises.description: A kneeling side bend lengthens your side body and inner thigh while building awareness of lateral movement.
steps: Kneel tall and extend one leg sideways with the foot flat.
Rest the hand nearest your extended leg lightly on that shin.
Reach your other arm overhead and bend sideways over your extended leg.
Inhale along your upper ribs; exhale into a gentle side bend.
exercises.cue: Lengthen both sides of your waist.
exercises.tip: Pad your kneeling knee with a folded blanket and make the side bend smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg extend to the side from kneeling, then the body curve sideways over that leg as the top arm reaches overhead.
exercises.name: Gate Pose · Right

exercises.description: A kneeling side bend lengthens your side body and inner thigh while building awareness of lateral movement.
steps: Kneel tall and extend one leg sideways with the foot flat.
Rest the hand nearest your extended leg lightly on that shin.
Reach your other arm overhead and bend sideways over your extended leg.
Inhale along your upper ribs; exhale into a gentle side bend.
exercises.cue: Lengthen both sides of your waist.
exercises.tip: Pad your kneeling knee with a folded blanket and make the side bend smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg extend to the side from kneeling, then the body curve sideways over that leg as the top arm reaches overhead.
exercises.name: Gate Pose · Left

exercises.description: A seated hip hinge stretches the backs of your legs while developing controlled length through your spine.
steps: Sit with your legs extended together and feet flexed.
Lengthen your spine and hinge forward from your hips.
Hold your shins or feet without pulling, keeping your neck in line with your back.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale to fold only as far as your breath stays easy.
exercises.cue: Keep space through your spine.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees and sit on a folded blanket to make the forward hinge easier.
exercises.watch: Watch the spine lengthen up first, then the body fold forward from the hips, keeping space in the back rather than rounding hard.
exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold

exercises.description: An asymmetrical seated fold stretches one hamstring at a time while developing a steady, deliberate hip hinge.
steps: Sit with one leg extended and bend your other knee outward.
Place the bent leg’s sole against your inner thigh and face your extended leg.
Lengthen forward from your hips and hold your extended shin or foot gently.
Breathe into your back, easing forward on each exhale without pulling.
exercises.cue: Fold toward your leg without forcing your head down.
exercises.tip: Bend your extended knee and support the bent knee with a folded blanket.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg stay long and the other foot rest on the inner thigh, then the chest turns toward the long leg and folds.
exercises.name: Head-to-Knee Fold · Right

exercises.description: An asymmetrical seated fold stretches one hamstring at a time while developing a steady, deliberate hip hinge.
steps: Sit with one leg extended and bend your other knee outward.
Place the bent leg’s sole against your inner thigh and face your extended leg.
Lengthen forward from your hips and hold your extended shin or foot gently.
Breathe into your back, easing forward on each exhale without pulling.
exercises.cue: Fold toward your leg without forcing your head down.
exercises.tip: Bend your extended knee and support the bent knee with a folded blanket.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg stay long and the other foot rest on the inner thigh, then the chest turns toward the long leg and folds.
exercises.name: Head-to-Knee Fold · Left

exercises.description: A wide seated fold explores inner thigh and hamstring length while developing awareness of your pelvis.
steps: Sit with your legs extended in a comfortable V.
Point your kneecaps and toes upward and place your hands in front of you.
Hinge forward from your hips, walking your hands along the mat.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale to walk your hands slightly farther only if comfortable.
exercises.cue: Keep your kneecaps facing upward.
exercises.tip: Sit on a folded blanket, narrow your leg position, and keep a small bend in your knees.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs open into a wide V with the kneecaps facing up, then the hands walk forward as the spine stays long.
exercises.name: Wide-Angle Seated Fold

exercises.description: This seated rotation combines a tall spine with a grounded base, developing controlled spinal movement.
steps: Sit with one leg folded, heel near the opposite hip.
Plant your other foot outside the folded knee and sit tall.
Turn toward your raised knee, placing the opposite elbow outside it and your other hand behind you.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale into a small twist without levering against your knee.
exercises.cue: Grow tall before turning.
exercises.tip: Keep your bottom leg extended and hug the raised knee instead of hooking your elbow.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit tall first, then turn from the belly, with one arm hugging the knee and the other hand behind for support.
exercises.name: Half Lord of the Fishes · Right

exercises.description: This seated rotation combines a tall spine with a grounded base, developing controlled spinal movement.
steps: Sit with one leg folded, heel near the opposite hip.
Plant your other foot outside the folded knee and sit tall.
Turn toward your raised knee, placing the opposite elbow outside it and your other hand behind you.
Inhale to lengthen; exhale into a small twist without levering against your knee.
exercises.cue: Grow tall before turning.
exercises.tip: Keep your bottom leg extended and hug the raised knee instead of hooking your elbow.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit tall first, then turn from the belly, with one arm hugging the knee and the other hand behind for support.
exercises.name: Half Lord of the Fishes · Left

exercises.description: A reclined twist explores gentle rotation while your shoulders rest on the mat.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Open your arms into a T and lower both knees together to one side.
Rest both shoulders down and turn your head away from your knees if comfortable.
Breathe slowly, letting your knees settle without pushing them down.
exercises.cue: Let your shoulders rest heavy.
exercises.tip: Place a pillow under your knees and keep your head facing upward if turning feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees fall to one side while both shoulders stay heavy on the mat and the gaze turns the other way.
exercises.name: Supine Spinal Twist · Right

exercises.description: A reclined twist explores gentle rotation while your shoulders rest on the mat.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Open your arms into a T and lower both knees together to one side.
Rest both shoulders down and turn your head away from your knees if comfortable.
Breathe slowly, letting your knees settle without pushing them down.
exercises.cue: Let your shoulders rest heavy.
exercises.tip: Place a pillow under your knees and keep your head facing upward if turning feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees fall to one side while both shoulders stay heavy on the mat and the gaze turns the other way.
exercises.name: Supine Spinal Twist · Left

exercises.description: Staff Pose is an upright seated foundation that builds postural endurance and active awareness through your legs.
steps: Sit with your legs extended together in front of you.
Flex your feet and place your palms beside your hips.
Press gently through your hands and lengthen upward, relaxing your shoulders.
Breathe evenly while keeping your chest lifted and your jaw soft.
exercises.cue: Lift through your crown without stiffening your shoulders.
exercises.tip: Sit on a folded blanket and bend your knees slightly.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs stretch long with the toes pointing up, the hands press down beside the hips, and the spine sit tall.
exercises.name: Staff Pose

exercises.description: A simple cross-legged seat builds upright sitting awareness and offers a steady place to notice your breath.
steps: Sit cross-legged with your weight balanced across your sitting bones.
Rest your hands on your knees, palms facing upward.
Lengthen your spine and relax your shoulders; soften or close your eyes.
Follow the gentle rise and fall of your belly and chest.
exercises.cue: Sit tall with an easy jaw.
exercises.tip: Raise your hips on a cushion, or sit in a sturdy chair with your feet supported.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs cross comfortably, the sitting bones ground, and the spine grow tall with the shoulders and jaw relaxed.
exercises.name: Easy Pose

exercises.description: A supported kneeling twist stretches the shoulder and upper back while inviting quieter attention.
steps: Begin on hands and knees with your hips above your knees.
Slide one arm beneath your chest toward the opposite side, palm upward.
Rest that shoulder and the side of your head down; keep your other hand planted forward.
Breathe slowly, softening into the supported shoulder without pressing through your head.
exercises.cue: Keep weight off your neck.
exercises.tip: Place a folded blanket under your shoulder and head, keeping your neck comfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch one arm slide under the body from all fours, so the shoulder and cheek rest down and the upper back gently twists.
exercises.name: Thread the Needle · Right

exercises.description: A supported kneeling twist stretches the shoulder and upper back while inviting quieter attention.
steps: Begin on hands and knees with your hips above your knees.
Slide one arm beneath your chest toward the opposite side, palm upward.
Rest that shoulder and the side of your head down; keep your other hand planted forward.
Breathe slowly, softening into the supported shoulder without pressing through your head.
exercises.cue: Keep weight off your neck.
exercises.tip: Place a folded blanket under your shoulder and head, keeping your neck comfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch one arm slide under the body from all fours, so the shoulder and cheek rest down and the upper back gently twists.
exercises.name: Thread the Needle · Left

exercises.description: This kneeling fold offers a grounded pause and brings awareness to the movement of breath across your back.
steps: Kneel with your big toes touching and knees slightly apart.
Ease your hips toward your heels and fold over your thighs.
Rest your forehead down and extend your arms forward, palms on the mat.
Let your back widen on each inhale and soften on each exhale.
exercises.cue: Let your forehead rest without straining your neck.
exercises.tip: Place a pillow between your thighs and torso, or a folded blanket behind your knees.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips sink back toward the heels, the arms rest long or beside the body, and the forehead rest on the mat.
exercises.name: Child’s Pose

exercises.description: Thunderbolt Pose is a heel-sitting posture that develops upright sitting awareness and steady attention.
steps: Kneel with your knees together and the tops of your feet on the mat.
Lower your hips onto your heels without forcing your knees or ankles.
Rest your hands on your thighs and lengthen through your crown.
Breathe evenly, keeping your shoulders relaxed and your face soft.
exercises.cue: Choose comfort over a lower seat.
exercises.tip: Place a folded blanket between your hips and heels, or choose a chair if kneeling feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the knees come together and the hips sit back onto the heels, with the spine tall and the hands resting on the thighs.
exercises.name: Thunderbolt Pose

exercises.description: A fully reclined rest gives you time to settle and practice letting go of unnecessary effort.
steps: Lie on your back and arrange your body for comfort.
Extend your legs, letting your feet fall open, and rest your arms slightly away from your body.
Turn your palms upward and soften your face; close your eyes if comfortable.
Rest quietly and allow your breath to move naturally.
exercises.cue: Let the floor carry your weight.
exercises.tip: Place a pillow under your knees and a folded blanket under your head if that feels more comfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch her lie back with the legs long, the feet falling open, and the palms facing up. Nothing to do now but rest.
exercises.name: Final Relaxation

exercises.description: A gentle reclined tuck explores hip flexion and small movements coordinated with your breath.
steps: Lie comfortably on your back with your head resting down.
Bring both knees toward your chest and hold your shins gently.
Relax your shoulders and leave room for your belly to move.
Exhale to draw your knees slightly closer; inhale to let them float away.
exercises.cue: Leave space for an easy breath.
exercises.tip: Hold behind your thighs instead of your shins and place a folded blanket under your head.
exercises.watch: Watch both knees draw in toward the chest while the lower back and shoulders rest heavy on the mat.
exercises.name: Knees to Chest

exercises.description: A reclined, open-knee rest invites comfortable stillness and awareness of your breathing.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Bring your soles together and allow your knees to open comfortably.
Rest one hand on your belly and one on your chest; soften or close your eyes.
Let your hands rise and fall with your natural breath.
exercises.cue: Support your legs enough to soften completely.
exercises.tip: Place pillows under both thighs and a folded blanket under your head for extra comfort.
exercises.watch: Watch the soles of the feet join, the knees fall open, and the arms rest wide, letting the body be completely supported.
exercises.name: Reclined Bound Angle

exercises.description: A wall-supported reclined rest lets your legs settle while you practice quiet attention.
steps: Sit beside the wall, then roll onto your back and swing your legs upward.
Rest your legs along the wall, choosing a comfortable distance for your hips.
Settle your arms out to your sides, palms upward, and soften or close your eyes.
Rest still and let your belly rise and fall naturally.
exercises.cue: Choose a wall distance that lets your legs relax.
exercises.tip: Move your hips farther from the wall and place a folded blanket under your head if helpful.
exercises.watch: Watch the hips come close to the wall, the legs rest straight up it, and the arms relax beside the body.
exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall

exercises.description: An upright, quiet butterfly explores a modest inner thigh stretch through patient stillness rather than active effort.
steps: Sit with your soles together near your pelvis and your knees open.
Hold your feet lightly and settle into a modest edge with your spine comfortably upright.
Soften your legs; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then bring your knees together with your hands and come out slowly.
exercises.cue: Let gravity work; do not press your knees.
exercises.tip: Support your thighs with cushions and sit on a folded blanket so your upright seat takes less effort.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit upright with the soles together and the hands resting on the feet, then simply stay still and let time do the work.
exercises.name: Yin Butterfly

exercises.description: A quiet seated fold explores the backs of your legs with soft muscles, modest sensation, and time.
steps: Sit with your legs extended together and your feet gently flexed.
Fold from your hips to a modest edge, resting your hands on your shins or feet.
Soften your muscles; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then use your hands for support and come upright slowly.
exercises.cue: Stay with a modest edge, not a deeper fold.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees over a pillow and sit on a folded blanket to reduce the stretch.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs stay long and the body fold only to a modest edge, then the muscles soften and stay still.
exercises.name: Caterpillar

exercises.description: A low, wide lunge becomes a quiet exploration of the hips, emphasizing modest sensation rather than muscular effort.
steps: From hands and knees, step one foot outside the hand on that side.
Lower your back knee, keep both hands inside your front foot, and find a modest edge.
Soften unnecessary muscular effort; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then shift your hips back and return to kneeling slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep the sensation modest and your front knee comfortable.
exercises.tip: Pad your back knee and place your hands on blocks to keep your hips higher.
exercises.watch: Watch the front foot step outside the hand, the back knee lower, and the hips settle down slowly into stillness.
exercises.name: Dragon · Right

exercises.description: A low, wide lunge becomes a quiet exploration of the hips, emphasizing modest sensation rather than muscular effort.
steps: From hands and knees, step one foot outside the hand on that side.
Lower your back knee, keep both hands inside your front foot, and find a modest edge.
Soften unnecessary muscular effort; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then shift your hips back and return to kneeling slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep the sensation modest and your front knee comfortable.
exercises.tip: Pad your back knee and place your hands on blocks to keep your hips higher.
exercises.watch: Watch the front foot step outside the hand, the back knee lower, and the hips settle down slowly into stillness.
exercises.name: Dragon · Left

exercises.description: A low forearm-supported backbend invites quiet attention to the front body and a modest curve through your back.
steps: Lie on your belly with your legs extended and tops of your feet resting down.
Place your forearms parallel, elbows beneath shoulders, and lift your chest to a modest edge.
Soften your legs and belly; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then lower your chest slowly and rest your head on your hands.
exercises.cue: Keep the curve modest and your face soft.
exercises.tip: Slide your elbows farther forward to lower your chest and reduce the curve in your back.
exercises.watch: Watch the forearms settle under the shoulders, the chest rise just a little, and the legs and belly completely relax.
exercises.name: Yin Sphinx

exercises.description: A wide seated fold explores the inner thighs through soft muscles, a modest edge, and patient stillness.
