steps: Sit with your legs extended in a comfortable V, toes and kneecaps upward.
Walk your hands forward and fold gently to a modest edge.
Soften your muscles; stay still for two to five minutes and let gravity work.
Breathe naturally, then walk your hands back and come upright slowly before bringing your legs together.
exercises.cue: Let time, not effort, shape the fold.
exercises.tip: Narrow your legs, bend your knees slightly, and support your torso on a pillow.
exercises.watch: Watch the legs open into a comfortable V, the hands walk forward a little, and the body rest at a gentle edge.
exercises.name: Dragonfly

exercises.description: A grounded chair seat builds postural awareness and gives your breath room to move.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Place your feet hip-width apart with your knees above your ankles.
Rest your hands on your thighs and lift through your crown, relaxing your shoulders.
Breathe gently, noticing your chest rise and settle.
exercises.cue: Grow tall without stiffening.
exercises.tip: Place firm support under your feet if they do not reach the floor comfortably.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit near the front of the chair, feet flat and hip-width apart, the spine tall and the hands resting on the thighs.
exercises.name: Seated Mountain

exercises.description: A seated spinal wave links a small arch and rounding movement with your breath, developing comfortable mobility.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Place your hands on your knees and begin with a tall, neutral spine.
Inhale and gently arch your back, lifting your chest forward and upward.
Exhale and round your back, drawing your belly inward and chin toward your chest.
Return to sitting tall and repeat within an easy range.
exercises.cue: Let your breath set the movement pace.
exercises.tip: Keep both movements small and your gaze near level if lowering or lifting your head feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands rest on the knees as the chest opens forward with the in-breath and the back rounds with the out-breath.
exercises.name: Seated Cat–Cow

exercises.description: A supported seated side bend creates length along your ribs while building awareness of your sitting base.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Rest one hand on the seat beside your hip and reach your other arm overhead.
Bend toward your supporting hand, keeping both sitting bones on the seat.
Inhale to lengthen your raised arm; exhale into a small side bend.
exercises.cue: Keep both sitting bones grounded.
exercises.tip: Keep your raised hand on your hip and make the side bend smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch one arm reach up and over while both sitting bones stay grounded on the chair.
exercises.name: Seated Side Bend · Right

exercises.description: A supported seated side bend creates length along your ribs while building awareness of your sitting base.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Rest one hand on the seat beside your hip and reach your other arm overhead.
Bend toward your supporting hand, keeping both sitting bones on the seat.
Inhale to lengthen your raised arm; exhale into a small side bend.
exercises.cue: Keep both sitting bones grounded.
exercises.tip: Keep your raised hand on your hip and make the side bend smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch one arm reach up and over while both sitting bones stay grounded on the chair.
exercises.name: Seated Side Bend · Left

exercises.description: A seated rotation develops controlled spinal movement while your feet and chair provide a steady base.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Place one hand outside the opposite knee and your other hand behind you on the seat.
Lengthen your spine and turn toward your rear hand, keeping your knees facing forward.
Inhale to sit taller; exhale into a small turn without pulling against the chair.
exercises.cue: Turn gently; keep your knees facing forward.
exercises.tip: Keep both hands on your thighs and use a smaller turn.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit tall, then turn from the belly toward the back of the chair, with the knees still facing forward.
exercises.name: Seated Twist · Right

exercises.description: A seated rotation develops controlled spinal movement while your feet and chair provide a steady base.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Place one hand outside the opposite knee and your other hand behind you on the seat.
Lengthen your spine and turn toward your rear hand, keeping your knees facing forward.
Inhale to sit taller; exhale into a small turn without pulling against the chair.
exercises.cue: Turn gently; keep your knees facing forward.
exercises.tip: Keep both hands on your thighs and use a smaller turn.
exercises.watch: Watch her sit tall, then turn from the belly toward the back of the chair, with the knees still facing forward.
exercises.name: Seated Twist · Left

exercises.description: A chair-supported fold invites your back, neck, and arms to soften while you explore a comfortable forward hinge.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Widen your feet and knees to make room for your torso.
Fold over your thighs, letting your head and arms hang between your knees toward the floor.
Breathe into your back and soften with each exhale without forcing a deeper fold.
exercises.cue: Fold only as far as your breath stays easy.
exercises.tip: Rest your forearms on your thighs and keep your head lifted for a smaller fold.
exercises.watch: Watch the body fold slowly over the thighs, the head and arms hanging heavy, with the feet flat on the floor.
exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold

exercises.description: A seated figure four explores the outer hip through a supported, controlled forward hinge.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Cross one ankle above the opposite knee and flex your crossed foot.
Rest your hands on your crossed shin and hinge slightly forward with a long spine.
Exhale into a gentle hip stretch without pressing your raised knee downward.
exercises.cue: Hinge from your hips; keep your crossed knee comfortable.
exercises.tip: Stay upright or cross your ankle lower on the supporting shin, keeping the supporting foot planted.
exercises.watch: Watch one ankle rest on the opposite knee, then the chest hinge forward from the hips, keeping the back long.
exercises.name: Seated Figure Four · Right

exercises.description: A seated figure four explores the outer hip through a supported, controlled forward hinge.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Cross one ankle above the opposite knee and flex your crossed foot.
Rest your hands on your crossed shin and hinge slightly forward with a long spine.
Exhale into a gentle hip stretch without pressing your raised knee downward.
exercises.cue: Hinge from your hips; keep your crossed knee comfortable.
exercises.tip: Stay upright or cross your ankle lower on the supporting shin, keeping the supporting foot planted.
exercises.watch: Watch one ankle rest on the opposite knee, then the chest hinge forward from the hips, keeping the back long.
exercises.name: Seated Figure Four · Left

exercises.description: This supported warrior shape combines a wide leg position with reaching arms, building seated stability and upper body endurance.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Rest one thigh on the seat, knee bent; extend your other leg sideways and back, foot flat.
Reach both arms outward at shoulder height and look over the fingertips above your bent knee.
Breathe steadily and grow tall while keeping your chair and feet stable.
exercises.cue: Let the chair support your weight.
exercises.tip: Keep your extended knee bent and your hands on your thighs for a smaller shape.
exercises.watch: Watch her turn sideways on the chair, one leg bent in front and one leg long behind, with the arms reaching wide.
exercises.name: Seated Warrior II · Right

exercises.description: This supported warrior shape combines a wide leg position with reaching arms, building seated stability and upper body endurance.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Rest one thigh on the seat, knee bent; extend your other leg sideways and back, foot flat.
Reach both arms outward at shoulder height and look over the fingertips above your bent knee.
Breathe steadily and grow tall while keeping your chair and feet stable.
exercises.cue: Let the chair support your weight.
exercises.tip: Keep your extended knee bent and your hands on your thighs for a smaller shape.
exercises.watch: Watch her turn sideways on the chair, one leg bent in front and one leg long behind, with the arms reaching wide.
exercises.name: Seated Warrior II · Left

exercises.description: Wrapped arms stretch the upper back while a supported seat helps you explore shoulder movement.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Cross one elbow beneath the other and wrap your forearms until your palms meet.
Lift your elbows toward shoulder height, keeping your neck long.
Inhale to lift slightly; exhale to soften your shoulders away from your ears.
exercises.cue: Lift your elbows without lifting your shoulders.
exercises.tip: Place your hands on opposite shoulders for a gentle self-hug instead of wrapping your forearms.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms cross and wrap at the elbows, then the elbows lift a little while the shoulders stay down.
exercises.name: Seated Eagle Arms

exercises.description: A small seated head tilt explores the side of your neck while you practice keeping your shoulders relaxed.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Tilt one ear gently toward the shoulder on that side.
Rest that hand lightly on the opposite side of your head; let your other arm hang.
Breathe slowly, keeping your shoulders level and your hand free of pulling pressure.
exercises.cue: Let your hand rest; never pull your head.
exercises.tip: Leave both hands on your thighs and make the head tilt smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch the head tip gently to one side, the hand resting lightly on top, and the opposite shoulder melting down.
exercises.name: Seated Neck Release · Right

exercises.description: A small seated head tilt explores the side of your neck while you practice keeping your shoulders relaxed.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Tilt one ear gently toward the shoulder on that side.
Rest that hand lightly on the opposite side of your head; let your other arm hang.
Breathe slowly, keeping your shoulders level and your hand free of pulling pressure.
exercises.cue: Let your hand rest; never pull your head.
exercises.tip: Leave both hands on your thighs and make the head tilt smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch the head tip gently to one side, the hand resting lightly on top, and the opposite shoulder melting down.
exercises.name: Seated Neck Release · Left

exercises.description: A seated arm sweep and forward fold link movement with breath, developing coordination through an accessible seated flow.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Inhale and sweep your arms outward and overhead.
Exhale and fold over your thighs, reaching your hands toward the floor.
Inhale and rise upright, sweeping your arms overhead again.
Exhale and lower your hands to your thighs; repeat at your own pace.
exercises.breath: Inhale rise · exhale fold or lower
exercises.cue: Keep your feet grounded throughout the flow.
exercises.tip: Lift your arms only as high as comfortable and rest your hands on your thighs during a smaller fold.
exercises.watch: Watch the arms float up as she breathes in, and fold forward over the legs as she breathes out, feet grounded.
exercises.name: Seated Sun Breath

exercises.description: A supported seated hinge stretches the back of one leg while developing awareness of a long spine.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Extend one leg forward, heel grounded and toes upward; keep your other foot flat.
Rest both hands on your bent thigh and hinge forward over your extended leg.
Inhale to lengthen your spine; exhale into a small hinge without rounding your back.
exercises.cue: Lead forward with your chest.
exercises.tip: Bend your extended knee slightly and keep your torso more upright.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg extend forward with the heel on the floor and the toes up, then the chest leans forward with a long spine.
exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch · Right

exercises.description: A supported seated hinge stretches the back of one leg while developing awareness of a long spine.
steps: Sit toward the front of a sturdy chair without wheels, feet flat.
Extend one leg forward, heel grounded and toes upward; keep your other foot flat.
Rest both hands on your bent thigh and hinge forward over your extended leg.
Inhale to lengthen your spine; exhale into a small hinge without rounding your back.
exercises.cue: Lead forward with your chest.
exercises.tip: Bend your extended knee slightly and keep your torso more upright.
exercises.watch: Watch one leg extend forward with the heel on the floor and the toes up, then the chest leans forward with a long spine.
exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch · Left

exercises.description: A wall-supported hinge lengthens your back and shoulders while building awareness of a steady hip hinge.
steps: Face the wall and place your palms against it at hip height.
Step back and hinge at your hips until your arms and torso are parallel to the floor.
Keep your feet beneath your hips, arms straight, and head between your upper arms.
Inhale to lengthen your spine; exhale to soften your chest toward the floor.
exercises.cue: Reach your hips back and your hands forward.
exercises.tip: Bend your knees and place your hands higher on the wall for a smaller hinge.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands press on the wall at hip height, then she walks back until the body forms an L, with a long spine.
exercises.name: Wall Downward Dog

exercises.description: A wall-supported squat builds leg and trunk endurance while you hold a steady seated shape.
steps: Stand with your back against the wall and step your feet forward, hip-width apart.
Slide down until your knees are above your ankles, working toward thighs parallel to the floor.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height and keep your back supported against the wall.
Breathe evenly, maintaining steady feet and a relaxed jaw.
exercises.cue: Keep your knees aligned above your ankles.
exercises.tip: Stay higher on the wall and rest your hands on your thighs to reduce the effort.
exercises.watch: Watch the back slide down the wall until the knees are bent over the ankles, as if sitting on an invisible chair.
exercises.name: Wall Chair

exercises.description: A standing wall stretch explores the front of your shoulder through a small, controlled turn.
steps: Stand beside the wall and place the nearer palm against it at shoulder height.
Keep that arm straight and turn your chest gently away, leaving your hand behind you.
Relax your shoulders and stop at a mild stretch across your chest.
Breathe slowly, turning only a little farther on an exhale if comfortable.
exercises.cue: Choose a mild stretch, not a strong pull.
exercises.tip: Place your hand lower and make the turn smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch the palm rest on the wall at shoulder height, then the body turn gently away until the chest opens.
exercises.name: Wall Chest Opener · Right

exercises.description: A standing wall stretch explores the front of your shoulder through a small, controlled turn.
steps: Stand beside the wall and place the nearer palm against it at shoulder height.
Keep that arm straight and turn your chest gently away, leaving your hand behind you.
Relax your shoulders and stop at a mild stretch across your chest.
Breathe slowly, turning only a little farther on an exhale if comfortable.
exercises.cue: Choose a mild stretch, not a strong pull.
exercises.tip: Place your hand lower and make the turn smaller.
exercises.watch: Watch the palm rest on the wall at shoulder height, then the body turn gently away until the chest opens.
exercises.name: Wall Chest Opener · Left

exercises.description: A wall-supported balance develops standing leg stability and trunk control while your lifted leg reaches backward.
steps: Face the wall and place both palms against it at hip height.
Step back and hinge forward until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Shift onto one leg and lift the other back, keeping your hips level.
Inhale to reach through your lifted heel; exhale to steady your balance.
exercises.cue: Keep both hip points facing the floor.
exercises.tip: Keep your lifted toes on the floor behind you and use a smaller forward hinge.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands rest on the wall as the body tips forward and one leg lifts back, making a T with both hips level.
exercises.name: Wall Warrior III · Right

exercises.description: A wall-supported balance develops standing leg stability and trunk control while your lifted leg reaches backward.
steps: Face the wall and place both palms against it at hip height.
Step back and hinge forward until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Shift onto one leg and lift the other back, keeping your hips level.
Inhale to reach through your lifted heel; exhale to steady your balance.
exercises.cue: Keep both hip points facing the floor.
exercises.tip: Keep your lifted toes on the floor behind you and use a smaller forward hinge.
exercises.watch: Watch the hands rest on the wall as the body tips forward and one leg lifts back, making a T with both hips level.
exercises.name: Wall Warrior III · Left

exercises.description: A lightly supported standing balance develops focus and steadiness through your standing leg.
steps: Stand beside the wall and rest your nearer fingertips against it.
Shift onto the leg nearest the wall and open your other knee outward.
Place your sole above or below the knee; rest your free hand at your chest.
Breathe softly, lengthen upward, and keep your gaze steady.
exercises.cue: Press your foot above or below the knee, never against it.
exercises.tip: Keep your raised toes on the floor with your heel against your standing ankle, using the wall for support.
exercises.watch: Watch one hand rest on the wall for support while the other foot rises to the inner calf or thigh, never the knee.
exercises.name: Wall Tree Pose · Right

exercises.description: A lightly supported standing balance develops focus and steadiness through your standing leg.
steps: Stand beside the wall and rest your nearer fingertips against it.
Shift onto the leg nearest the wall and open your other knee outward.
Place your sole above or below the knee; rest your free hand at your chest.
Breathe softly, lengthen upward, and keep your gaze steady.
exercises.cue: Press your foot above or below the knee, never against it.
exercises.tip: Keep your raised toes on the floor with your heel against your standing ankle, using the wall for support.
exercises.watch: Watch one hand rest on the wall for support while the other foot rises to the inner calf or thigh, never the knee.
exercises.name: Wall Tree Pose · Left

exercises.description: Three-Part Breath explores a smooth inhale through the belly, ribs, and upper chest, developing breath awareness without forcing capacity.
steps: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine, one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Inhale through your nose for four counts, letting your belly, ribs, then upper chest expand gently.
Exhale through your nose for six counts, allowing your chest, ribs, and belly to soften.
Repeat without forcing fullness; never strain, and return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.cue: Let expansion be gentle, not maximal.
exercises.tip: Sit on a cushion and shorten the counts if the rhythm feels effortful.
exercises.watch: Watch the breath fill three spaces in order: first the belly, then the ribs, then the upper chest, and empty slowly.
exercises.name: Three-Part Breath

exercises.description: Ujjayi adds a soft, whispering texture to nasal breathing, developing a steady rhythm and focused listening.
steps: Sit cross-legged, spine tall, hands on knees, touching each thumb to its index finger.
Close your lips and lightly narrow the back of your throat, creating a quiet whispering breath.
Inhale through your nose for four counts; exhale through your nose for four counts.
Keep the sound soft; never strain, and return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.cue: Keep your throat soft and your breath quiet.
exercises.tip: Release the throat texture and use ordinary nasal breathing if creating the sound feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch how calm the face stays: the breath moves slowly through the nose, with a soft ocean sound at the back of the throat.
exercises.name: Ujjayi Breath

exercises.description: Alternate Nostril Breathing uses gentle hand placement and an even rhythm to develop breath coordination and focused attention.
steps: Sit cross-legged; rest your left hand on your knee and fold your right index and middle fingers.
Close your right nostril with your right thumb; inhale through your left nostril for four counts.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger; release your thumb and exhale right for four counts.
Inhale right for four; close right, release left, and exhale left for four; repeat.
Never strain; return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.breath: Inhale four · exhale four · alternate nostrils
exercises.cue: Touch lightly; keep your face relaxed.
exercises.tip: Use ordinary nasal breathing with both nostrils open if either nostril feels blocked or the hand position is uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the right hand gently close one nostril at a time, breathing in one side and out the other, with a soft face.
exercises.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing

exercises.description: Box Breathing follows four equal phases, building a clear rhythm for steady attention.
steps: Sit cross-legged, spine tall, hands in your lap, one palm on the other, thumbs touching.
Inhale gently through your nose for four counts.
Hold your breath softly for four counts, without tightening your face.
Exhale for four counts, then hold gently for four counts before repeating.
Never strain; return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.cue: Keep every phase easy and equal.
exercises.tip: Shorten all four phases equally, or skip the holds and use natural breathing if pauses feel uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the steady rhythm: breathe in for four, hold for four, breathe out for four, and hold for four.
exercises.name: Box Breathing

exercises.description: Bee Breath pairs a gentle nasal inhale with a soft humming exhale, developing awareness of sound and vibration.
steps: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine and gently close your eyes if comfortable.
Rest your index fingers lightly on your ear flaps, elbows outward; apply no pressure.
Inhale through your nose for four counts, keeping your lips softly closed.
Exhale with a soft hum for six counts, relaxing your face; repeat gently.
Never strain; return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.cue: Keep your hum soft and your touch light.
exercises.tip: Keep your hands on your thighs and shorten the hum if touching your ears or extending the exhale feels uncomfortable.
exercises.watch: Watch the fingers rest lightly over the ears and eyes, then a soft hum rides on each slow out-breath.
exercises.name: Bee Breath

exercises.description: This rhythmic breathing practice uses short active exhales and passive inhales to develop precise abdominal coordination and focused attention.
steps: Sit cross-legged, spine tall, one hand on your lower belly and the other on your knee.
Exhale briefly through your nose, drawing your lower belly inward; allow the inhale to happen passively.
Repeat about once per second for twenty to thirty exhales, keeping your face and shoulders still.
Pause for normal breathing between rounds; never strain, and return to normal breathing if dizzy.
exercises.breath: Active exhales, passive inhales · one per second
exercises.cue: Keep inhales passive and exhales brief.
exercises.tip: Skip if pregnant, with high blood pressure or heart conditions, or after recent abdominal surgery; use slow belly breathing instead.
exercises.watch: Watch the belly snap gently in on each short out-breath, while each in-breath happens by itself.
exercises.name: Skull-Shining Breath

flows.name: Half Sun Salutation
flows.watch: Six movements, one for each breath: reach up, fold, lift halfway, fold again, rise all the way up, and return to Mountain.
flows.go: Your turn. Stand tall at the top of your mat, feet grounded, hands at your heart.

flows.name: Gentle Sun Salutation
flows.watch: The beginner's Sun Salutation. Watch the knees lower before the chest, then a low Cobra, and five slow breaths in Downward Dog before she walks forward and rises.
flows.go: Your turn. Stand at the top of your mat. Move slowly, and let the breath set the pace.

flows.name: Sun Salutation A
flows.watch: One movement for every breath. Watch her reach up, fold, lift halfway, lower down with straight lines, open into Upward Dog, then rest in Downward Dog for five breaths before stepping forward and rising.
flows.go: Your turn. Stand tall at the top of your mat. Knees can always come down on the way to the floor.

flows.name: Sun Salutation B
flows.watch: Sun Salutation B adds Chair Pose and Warrior One. Watch the rhythm: Chair, fold, lower down, Upward Dog, Downward Dog, then Warrior One on the right, and again on the left, before five breaths in Downward Dog.
flows.go: Your turn. Feet together at the top of your mat. Let the breath lead every movement.

flows.name: Moon Salutation
flows.watch: The cooling Moon Salutation travels from side to side. Watch the crescent side bends, Goddess, Triangle, Pyramid and a low lunge to the right, a deep squat in the middle, and then the same shapes back to the left.
flows.go: Your turn. Stand in Mountain at the centre of your mat. Move slowly, like the moon.

plans.title: Yoga in 7 Days
plans.subtitle: 7 days · your strong, simple start
plans.description: Seven energising lessons that give you the backbone of a real yoga practice: standing poses, Downward Dog, the Warriors, your first Sun Salutation, hip openers and core. Each day teaches something new, then links it into a short flow — free, and yours to repeat.
benefits: A daily habit in a week
welcome: In seven short days you'll learn the backbone of a real yoga practice: the standing poses, Downward Dog, the Warriors, and your very first Sun Salutation.
No experience needed. Just a mat, a little space, and about fifteen minutes a day.
plans.finale: Seven days ago you started with Mountain Pose. Today you flowed a complete practice. Repeat this week whenever you like, or take your next step with Yoga Foundations.

days.title: Stand tall, breathe wide
days.intro: Today we build your foundation from the ground up: a tall Mountain Pose, your first forward folds, Chair Pose, and the strong, open stance of Warrior Two.

days.title: Meet Downward Dog
days.intro: Today you meet Downward-Facing Dog, the pose you'll come home to in almost every class, with Plank and Cobra to wake up your arms and back.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll meet Downward-Facing Dog, the shape you'll come back to in almost every yoga class.

days.title: Warriors & balance
days.intro: Today is about standing strong. We review Warrior Two, then learn Warrior One, Reverse Warrior and your first balance, Tree Pose.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we stand like warriors, and you'll find your very first balance in Tree Pose.

days.title: Your first Sun Salutation
days.intro: Today you link the pieces into your first Sun Salutation. The first round is slow, two breaths in every shape. Then you'll flow it, one breath for each movement.
days.tease: Tomorrow, the pieces you've learned link up into your very first Sun Salutation.

plans.title: Yoga Foundations
plans.subtitle: 21 days · learn the poses that matter
plans.description: A complete beginner curriculum in three weeks. Week one builds your standing poses and alignment, week two teaches Sun Salutations and the floor practice, week three adds balance, backbends and longer flows. Every lesson warms you up, reviews what you know, teaches one or two new poses and ends in rest.
welcome: Over three weeks, we'll build your yoga practice the way a good teacher would: one or two new poses a day, always on top of what you already know.
Week one is standing poses, week two is Sun Salutations and the floor, and week three brings balance, backbends and your own full practice.
plans.finale: Twenty-one days, and the foundations are yours: the standing poses, Sun Salutations, balance, backbends and rest. Your practice now belongs to you.

days.intro: Today we begin where every pose begins: Mountain. You'll learn to stand with intention, then move with your breath in your first Half Sun Salutation.

days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn Triangle and Side Angle, the long lines of classical yoga.

days.title: Week one: rest & restore

days.tease: Tomorrow is a rest day. Your body learns while it rests, so we'll keep it soft and slow.

days.title: Plank, Knees-Chest-Chin & Cobra

days.title: Sun Salutation, slowly
days.intro: Today you link it all into a Sun Salutation. One slow round with two breaths in each shape, then one round with a single breath per movement.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll link those pieces into a complete Sun Salutation.

plans.title: Daily Yoga
plans.subtitle: 28 days · energy, strength & flow
plans.description: A 20-minute flowing practice for every day of the month, in four themed weeks: energy, strength, flexibility and balance. Each day opens differently, builds heat with real breath-paced Sun Salutations, rises to a focused peak, and closes in a long rest — with a softer restore day at the end of every week.
welcome: This is your daily practice for the next four weeks: twenty minutes that open differently every day, build heat with Sun Salutations, and finish in deep rest.
Week one brings energy, week two strength, week three flexibility, and week four balance.
plans.finale: Twenty-eight days of practice. That's not a challenge any more, that's a habit. Keep the rhythm going, and let yoga be part of every day.

plans.title: Sun Salutation Journey
plans.subtitle: 14 days · master Surya Namaskar A & B
plans.description: Learn the two Sun Salutations at the heart of every flowing class, one piece at a time. Week one breaks Surya Namaskar A into its parts — reach, fold, plank, the low push-up, upward dog and Downward Dog — and links them with breath. Week two adds Chair Pose and Warrior I for Surya Namaskar B, then builds to five full rounds.
welcome: In two weeks you'll master the two Sun Salutations at the heart of every flowing class, one piece at a time.
Week one builds Sun Salutation A, shape by shape. Week two adds Chair Pose and Warrior One for Sun Salutation B, and builds to five full rounds.
plans.finale: From one reach and fold to five full rounds: you now know the Sun Salutations by heart. Greet the sun with them whenever you like.

plans.title: Strong Yoga
plans.subtitle: 21 days · power, core & stamina
plans.description: Power yoga for real strength: longer holds, plank work, standing endurance and optional arm-balance preparation. Keep knees down, use blocks or skip balances whenever your wrists or shoulders ask for it. Week one builds a strong core and legs, week two adds balance and stamina, week three links everything into powerful flows — with an easy mobility day each week.
welcome: This is power yoga for real strength: longer holds, plank work, standing endurance and your first arm balances.
Strength grows with recovery, so every week has an easy mobility day. And knees down is always a strong choice.
plans.finale: Three weeks of power yoga: a stronger core, stronger legs, and the stamina to flow for thirty minutes. That strength is yours now. Keep using it.

plans.title: Flexibility in 21 Days
plans.subtitle: 21 days · hamstrings, hips & spine
plans.description: A progressive stretching plan for the three places most of us feel tight. Each week rotates hamstring, hip and spine days with warm, active flows first so you stretch safely, and finishes with longer, quieter holds. By day 21 forward folds, lunges and twists feel genuinely different.
welcome: Over three weeks we'll work on the three places most of us feel tight: the hamstrings, the hips and the spine.
We always warm up first, we never force a stretch, and every week ends with long, quiet holds. By day twenty-one, you'll feel the difference.
plans.finale: Twenty-one days of patient stretching. Fold forward and notice how far you've come. Flexibility stays with the people who keep showing up, so keep showing up.

plans.title: Open Hips
plans.subtitle: 10 days · release tight hips
plans.description: Ten focused sessions for hips that sit all day. You warm up with lunges and squats, then explore the hip from every direction — front, outside, inside and rotation — with props-friendly options and long, calm holds to finish.
welcome: Ten sessions for hips that sit all day. We'll explore the hip from every direction: the front, the outside, the inner thighs, and rotation.
Cushions and blocks are welcome, and the long holds at the end of each day are where the real release happens.
plans.finale: Ten days, every direction of the hip explored. Sit down, stand up, take a step, and notice the freedom. Come back to these days whenever your hips feel tight.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we go to the outer hip with Figure Four and Pigeon.

days.intro: Today we explore the deep squat, the most natural hip opener there is, from Chair Pose down into Garland.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we explore the deep squat.

days.title: Hips in flow
days.intro: Today we warm the hips with moving Sun Salutations, then sink into Low Lunge and Pigeon.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we warm the hips with flowing Sun Salutations.

plans.title: Healthy Back
plans.subtitle: 14 days · mobility for everyday stiffness
plans.description: Two weeks of kind, intelligent movement for a back that sits, lifts and carries all day. Gentle spinal waves, core stability and hip release come first; strength for the back body and longer flows follow. Move within comfort, and check with a health professional if you have an injury.
welcome: Two weeks of kind, intelligent movement for a back that sits, lifts and carries all day.
We start with gentle spinal waves and a stable core, then build strength for the back body. Always move within comfort, and skip anything that pinches.
plans.finale: Fourteen days of caring for your back. Keep the routine from the last day as your daily ten minutes, and your back will thank you.

days.title: Spinal waves
days.intro: Today we simply move the spine, gently, in every direction: rounding, arching and a soft twist.

days.title: Stable core
days.intro: Today we find the deep core muscles that support your back, with Dead Bug and Bird Dog, slow and precise.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we find the deep core muscles that protect your back.

days.title: Release the hips
days.intro: Today we release the hips, because tight hips pull on the lower back.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we release the hips, which takes pressure off the lower back.

days.intro: Today we create length, from Child's Pose to Downward Dog to a flat-backed Halfway Lift.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we give the spine length.

days.intro: Today we gently strengthen the back muscles with Sphinx, Locust and Bridge.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we gently strengthen the back with Locust and Bridge.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we unwind with soft twists.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we practise good posture standing up.

days.tease: Tomorrow, week two begins: strength for the core and the back body.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we release the sides of the waist.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we lengthen the hamstrings, kindly, for the sake of the back.

days.title: Strong posture

days.tease: Tomorrow, we build the strength behind good posture.

days.title: Gentle flow

days.tease: Tomorrow, we move in a gentle, breath-led flow.

plans.title: Yin & Sleep
plans.subtitle: 14 evenings · slow down, sleep deeper
plans.description: An evening ritual of long, supported Yin holds, soft breathing and restorative shapes. Each night targets one area — hips, spine, legs or shoulders — then guides you into stillness, so your body and mind are ready for rest.
welcome: This is your evening ritual for the next two weeks: long, supported Yin holds, soft breathing and restful shapes.
Dim the lights, gather a pillow or two, and let each evening slow you down for sleep.
plans.finale: Fourteen evenings of slowing down. You now have a ritual that tells your body the day is done. Keep it for the nights you need it.

days.tease: Tomorrow evening, we soften the spine.

days.tease: Tomorrow evening: legs up, mind down.

plans.title: Breath of Yoga
plans.subtitle: 10 days · the classic pranayama
plans.description: Learn the breathing techniques yoga is built on: three-part breath, Ujjayi, alternate-nostril breathing, box breathing, Bhramari and an optional gentle Kapalabhati. Each day prepares the body, teaches one technique carefully and invites you to return to natural breathing whenever you feel light-headed, anxious or uncomfortable. Skip fast breathing during pregnancy or if you have a health concern.
welcome: In ten short days you'll learn the classic breathing techniques of yoga, called pranayama, one at a time.
If you ever feel light-headed or uneasy, simply return to your natural breath. That's always part of the practice.
plans.finale: Ten days, six classic breaths. Now you can calm down, wake up or focus, just by how you breathe. That's the quiet power of pranayama.

days.title: Three-part breath
days.intro: Today you learn the three-part breath, the foundation of every technique: belly, ribs and chest, filling and emptying slowly.

days.title: Ujjayi, the ocean breath
days.intro: Today you learn Ujjayi, the ocean breath: a soft sound at the back of the throat that slows and steadies everything.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn Ujjayi, the ocean breath.

days.title: Breath in movement
days.intro: Today we bring the breath into movement, letting Ujjayi lead every motion.
days.tease: Tomorrow, the breath begins to lead your movement.

days.title: Alternate-nostril breathing
days.intro: Today you learn Nadi Shodhana, alternate-nostril breathing, one of the most balancing techniques in yoga.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn alternate-nostril breathing.

days.title: Box breathing
days.intro: Today you learn box breathing: in, hold, out, hold, all for the same count. Simple, and wonderfully steadying.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn box breathing, calm in four equal counts.

days.title: Bee breath
days.intro: Today you learn Bhramari, the bee breath: a soft hum on every out-breath that quiets the mind.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn Bhramari, the humming bee breath.

days.title: Skull-shining breath
days.intro: Today you learn Kapalabhati, an energising breath of short, active out-breaths. Go gently, and skip it if you're pregnant or unsure.
days.tease: Tomorrow, you'll learn Kapalabhati, the energising breath.

days.title: Calming ladder
days.intro: Today we combine techniques to calm down step by step: Ujjayi, then box breathing.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we combine breaths into a calming ladder.

days.title: Energy & balance
days.intro: Today we pair energy with balance: Kapalabhati to wake up, then Nadi Shodhana to settle.
days.tease: Tomorrow, we pair an energising breath with a balancing one.

days.title: Your breath practice
days.intro: Today is your own breath practice: four techniques in one calm session you can return to every day.

plans.title: Chair Yoga
plans.subtitle: 21 days · seated, supported, effective
plans.description: Real yoga from a steady chair — ideal for desk days, travel, sensitive knees or anyone who prefers to stay seated. Three weeks build mobility, then strength and balance-friendly shapes, then flowing seated sequences with breathwork to finish every session.
welcome: This is real yoga from a steady chair: perfect for desk days, travel, sensitive knees, or simply when you'd rather stay seated.
Use a sturdy chair without wheels. Week one brings mobility, week two strength, and week three flowing seated sequences.
plans.finale: Twenty-one days of yoga from your chair. Your spine moves more freely, your shoulders sit lower, and your breath is easier. Keep a few minutes of it in every day.

plans.title: Wall Yoga
plans.subtitle: 14 days · supported strength & balance
plans.description: Use a wall as your teacher. It steadies your balance, shows you true alignment and makes strength work friendlier — from wall Downward Dog to wall-supported Warrior III and Tree. Each session ends with Legs Up the Wall, one of yoga’s most loved recovery shapes.
welcome: For the next two weeks, a wall becomes your teacher. It steadies your balance, shows you true alignment, and makes strength work friendlier.
Find a clear stretch of wall with space for your mat, and every session ends in Legs Up the Wall.
plans.finale: Fourteen days with the wall as your teacher. Your balance is steadier and your alignment clearer. Try Tree and Warrior Three away from the wall, and see how far you've come.

plans.title: Chakra Journey
plans.subtitle: 14 days · root to crown
plans.description: Travel up the spine through yoga's traditional map of seven chakras, two days for each: one moving practice with poses that suit the centre, and one quieter day of breath and stillness with its seed sound. Muladhara grounds you, Svadhisthana frees the hips, Manipura builds core warmth, Anahata opens the chest, Vishuddha eases the neck, Ajna steadies balance and focus, and Sahasrara brings it all together. The chakras are presented as a classic way to direct attention, not as a medical system.
benefits: Seed sounds & breath for each centre
welcome: Over fourteen days we'll travel up the spine through yoga's traditional map of the seven chakras, two days for each centre.
One day moves, the next is quieter, with breath and stillness. Think of the chakras as an ancient way to place your attention, from the ground beneath you to the crown of your head.
plans.finale: From root to crown, all seven centres explored. Grounded, open, warm and clear. Carry this map with you, and return to whichever centre you need.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we kindle Manipura, the inner fire, with core work and twists.

plans.title: The Eight Limbs
plans.subtitle: 8 days · Patanjali's path, lived
plans.description: Around two thousand years ago the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali described yoga as eight limbs: yama and niyama (how we treat the world and ourselves), asana (posture), pranayama (breath), pratyahara (turning inward), dharana (concentration), dhyana (meditation) and samadhi (absorption). Each day explores one limb through a practice built around it, from gentle non-forcing movement to steady balance and long, quiet rest.
welcome: About two thousand years ago, the sage Patanjali described yoga as a path with eight limbs. Postures are only one of them.
Over eight days, we'll live each limb through a practice built around it, from kindness and discipline to breath, focus and deep stillness.
plans.finale: Eight days, eight limbs. You've practised the whole of yoga, not just the poses. Patanjali would say the path continues every day, on and off the mat.

days.title: Yama · Practise without force
days.intro: The first limb is yama, how we treat the world, starting with ahimsa, non-harming. Today we practise without force, and stop before any pain.

days.title: Niyama · Steady daily effort
days.intro: The second limb is niyama, how we treat ourselves, including tapas, steady effort. Today we keep a calm, determined rhythm.
days.tease: Tomorrow, the second limb, niyama: steady, daily effort.

plans.title: Classical Hatha
plans.subtitle: 14 days · the traditional sequence
plans.description: Practise yoga the way it has been taught in the ashrams of Rishikesh for generations: opening breath, slow Sun Salutations, then the classical postures in their traditional order, each followed by rest, and pranayama before a long relaxation. Over two weeks you build the full sequence — fish, forward bend, cobra, locust, bow, the half spinal twist, crow and triangle — with gentle substitutes where headstand and shoulderstand would appear.
welcome: This is yoga as it has been taught in the ashrams of Rishikesh for generations: slow Sun Salutations, the classical postures in their traditional order, and deep rest between them.
Over two weeks we'll build the whole sequence, one family of poses at a time, with gentle substitutes for headstand and shoulderstand.
plans.finale: Fourteen days, and the classical Hatha sequence is yours, from the opening breath to the final relaxation. It has served students for generations. May it serve you too.

plans.title: Sun & Moon
plans.subtitle: 10 days · Surya and Chandra Namaskar
plans.description: Hatha is often explained as ha, the sun, and tha, the moon. This course alternates the two: warming solar days built on Surya Namaskar A and B, standing strength and an optional energising breath, and cooling lunar days built on Chandra Namaskar, the moon salutation, with wide hip openers and calming alternate-nostril breathing. The last day joins both in one balanced practice.
welcome: Hatha yoga is often explained as ha, the sun, and tha, the moon. Over ten days we'll alternate the two.
Sun days are warming and strong, built on Surya Namaskar. Moon days are cooling and open, built on Chandra Namaskar, the moon salutation.
plans.finale: Ten days of sun and moon. Now you can choose: warmth and energy when you need it, coolness and calm when you need that. Balance is knowing which one today asks for.

plans.title: Ashtanga Primer
plans.subtitle: 14 days · breath, posture, gaze
plans.description: An approachable introduction to Ashtanga vinyasa, the dynamic method taught by K. Pattabhi Jois in Mysore. You learn its three pillars, called tristhana — Ujjayi breath, posture and a steady gaze — then Sun Salutations A and B, the standing sequence and the seated forward bends, twists and hip openers of the primary series. Two rest days honour the tradition's rhythm of practice and recovery, and the final day links a half-primary practice you can keep.
benefits: The Ashtanga method, step by step
A practice you can repeat for years
welcome: This is an approachable introduction to Ashtanga, the dynamic method taught in Mysore by K. Pattabhi Jois.
You'll learn its three pillars, breath, posture and a steady gaze, then the Sun Salutations, the standing sequence and the seated poses, building to a half-primary practice you can keep for years.
plans.finale: Fourteen days, and you can practise the first half of the primary series. Ashtanga is meant to be repeated, so keep coming back to the last day. Breath, posture, gaze.

plans.title: Ayurveda & Yoga
plans.subtitle: 9 days · practice for vata, pitta and kapha
plans.description: Ayurveda, yoga's sister tradition, describes three doshas — vata (air and space), pitta (fire and water) and kapha (earth and water) — as qualities that shape how we feel. Here they guide the mood of each practice: three grounding, slow vata days, three cooling, non-competitive pitta days and three energising kapha days. Use them to match your practice to how you feel today. This course is a way to choose practice, not a diagnosis or treatment.
welcome: Ayurveda, yoga's sister tradition, describes three qualities, called doshas: vata, airy and quick; pitta, fiery and driven; and kapha, earthy and steady.
Each gets three days: grounding practice for vata, cooling practice for pitta, and energising practice for kapha. Afterwards, you'll know which practice suits how you feel today.
plans.finale: Nine days, three qualities. Restless? Choose a vata day. Heated? A pitta day. Heavy? A kapha day. That's Ayurveda's gift: practice that matches the day you're having.

days.intro: We begin with vata, the airy, restless quality. Today's practice is steady and grounding: strong standing poses held calmly.

days.tease: Tomorrow, we stay slow and warm.

days.title: Pitta · Cool the fire

days.tease: Tomorrow, we turn to pitta, and cool the fire.

items.c: Inhale, arms overhead, palms together.

Turn your hips to the right and fold over the front leg. Pyramid.
Lower your back knee. Low Lunge.
Bring your feet wide and sink into a deep squat. Garland Pose.
Turn to the left and lower into Low Lunge.
Straighten both legs. Pyramid on the left.
Open your hips. Triangle on the left.
Return to the centre. Goddess.
Step your feet together. Mountain, hands to your heart.
