meditations.title: Evening Wind-Down
meditations.subtitle: Let the day dissolve
meditations.about: A slow, lying-down practice that closes the day piece by piece. Use it in bed and let it fade into sleep.

script.text: Welcome. Lie down comfortably, let your head be supported, and allow your eyes to close.
The day is done. Whatever is unfinished can wait until morning.
Take a slow breath in through the nose, and let a long, soft breath out.
Feel the places where your body meets the bed: the back of the head, the shoulders, the hips, the heels.
Let the bed take a little more of your weight with every exhale.
Unclench the jaw. Let the tongue rest. Let the space between the eyebrows grow wide.
Let the shoulders slide away from the ears and rest heavy on the bed.
Picture the day as a long road behind you. You have arrived home.
If a thought pulls you back into the day, notice it kindly, and return to the feeling of the breath.
Breathing in, I am here. Breathing out, I let go.
Your hands are heavy. Your legs are heavy. Your face is soft.
There is nothing to fix and nowhere to be.
Let the breath become as slow and quiet as it wants to be.
Stay here as long as you like, and let sleep arrive in its own time.
Goodnight.

meditations.title: Deep Sleep Body Scan
meditations.subtitle: Release, part by part
meditations.about: A slow journey from the toes to the crown of the head, softening each part of the body. Ideal for nights when the body is tired but the mind is busy.

script.text: Lie on your back or on your side, whichever lets you rest most easily, and close your eyes.
We will travel slowly through the body. Wherever attention rests, let that place soften.
Begin with the toes of both feet. Notice them without moving them, and let them go.
The soles of the feet. The heels. The ankles. Let them grow warm and heavy.
Move up through the shins and calves, as if warm water were rising slowly around them.
The knees, and the backs of the knees. Let them be loose.
The thighs, front and back, sinking into the bed.
The hips and the pelvis, wide and heavy. Let the lower back melt down.
The belly rises and falls on its own. Let it be soft.
The chest, the ribs, the whole upper back, spreading across the bed.
Both arms, from the shoulders to the fingertips, heavy and still.
The neck, the throat, the back of the head resting completely.
The jaw, the lips, the cheeks. The eyes resting deep in their sockets. The forehead smooth.
Now feel the whole body at once, from toes to crown, warm, heavy and supported.
If you are still awake, simply keep breathing and feeling the body as one quiet shape.
Each exhale takes you a little deeper into rest.
You can let go of listening now.
There is nothing left to do. Rest, and drift.
Sleep well.

meditations.title: Evening Reflection
meditations.subtitle: Svadhyaya: look back with kindness
meditations.about: Svadhyaya, self-study, is one of the classic niyamas of yoga. This gentle review of the day lets you notice, learn and set the day down before sleep.

script.text: Sit or lie comfortably, and let your eyes close. Take three slow breaths to arrive.
In yoga, svadhyaya means self-study. Tonight we will look back on the day the way a kind friend would.
Picture this morning, the moment you woke. Notice how you felt, without judging it.
Let the day play forward slowly, like floating lamps drifting down a river.
Notice one moment that went well today, however small. Let yourself feel it again.
Notice one moment you would do differently. Ask, gently: what was I needing then?
Offer yourself the understanding you would offer someone you love.
Notice one person who helped you today, knowingly or not. Silently thank them.
Now let each moment of the day float on, out of sight, downstream.
Whatever happened, it has already become part of the river.
Rest in the quiet that remains. Breathing in, breathing out.
If you like, choose one simple intention for tomorrow, and then let it go too.
Let the breath slow down. Let the body grow heavy.
The day is complete. You can put it down now.
Rest well.

meditations.title: Yoga Nidra
meditations.subtitle: The deep, guided rest of yoga
meditations.about: Yoga Nidra, yogic sleep, is a classic guided relaxation that moves through intention, body rotation, breath and imagery. You stay softly aware while the body rests deeply.

script.text: Welcome to Yoga Nidra. Lie on your back, arms a little away from the body, palms turned up, and let the feet fall open.
Make any last adjustments now, so you can be completely still. Your only task is to listen and stay softly aware.
Notice the sounds around you, near and far. Let them come and go. Then become aware of the room, and your body lying in it.
Now choose your sankalpa, a short, positive intention in the present tense. Repeat it silently three times, with feeling.
We begin the rotation of awareness. Move your attention as I name each part, without moving the body.
Right hand thumb. Index finger. Middle finger. Ring finger. Little finger. The palm, the back of the hand, the wrist.
Right forearm, elbow, upper arm, shoulder. Right side of the waist, right hip, thigh, knee, shin, ankle. The right foot and all five toes.
Left hand thumb. Index finger. Middle finger. Ring finger. Little finger. The palm, the back of the hand, the wrist.
Left forearm, elbow, upper arm, shoulder. Left side of the waist, left hip, thigh, knee, shin, ankle. The left foot and all five toes.
The back of the body: heels, calves, backs of the thighs, buttocks, the whole spine, shoulder blades, the back of the head.
The front of the body: forehead, eyebrows, eyes, nose, cheeks, lips, chin, throat, chest, belly. The whole body together.
Now become aware of the natural breath, flowing in and out through the nostrils. Do not change it. Just watch.
Count each breath backward from twenty-seven. Breathing in, twenty-seven. Breathing out, twenty-seven. If you lose count, begin again.
Let the counting go. Now feel heaviness, as if the whole body were sinking deep into the earth.
Now feel lightness, as if the body were weightless, floating just above the floor.
Now feel warmth, like sunlight resting on the skin. And now coolness, like a breeze across the body at night.
Picture a wide calm lake at dawn. Mist rises slowly from the water. A single bird crosses the sky.
Picture a small lamp glowing steadily in a quiet temple. The flame does not flicker.
Picture the night sky, deep and full of stars, stretching on without end.
Let the images fade. Rest in the space behind the eyes, awake and completely relaxed.
Now repeat your sankalpa again, three times, with the same words as before. Let it sink deep inside.
Slowly become aware of the breath, the body, the floor beneath you, and the sounds of the room.
Begin to move your fingers and toes. When you are ready, roll to your right side, and come up slowly. Yoga Nidra is complete.

meditations.title: Yoga Nidra in 12
meditations.subtitle: A shorter yogic sleep
meditations.about: All the stages of Yoga Nidra in a shorter form, perfect for a midday reset or the end of a practice. Lie down somewhere you will not be disturbed.

script.text: Lie down on your back and make yourself comfortable. Let the arms rest by your sides, palms up.
For the next few minutes, stay still and stay listening. If you drift, simply return to my voice.
Silently repeat a short intention three times. Something simple and true, like: I am calm and steady.
Bring awareness to the right hand, the right arm, the right side of the body, all the way down to the right foot.
Bring awareness to the left hand, the left arm, the left side of the body, all the way down to the left foot.
Feel the whole back of the body resting. Feel the whole front of the body open to the air.
Feel the whole body together, still and quiet.
Watch the natural breath at the nostrils. Count ten breaths backward, from ten to one.
Feel the body heavy, sinking. Then light, floating. Then simply as it is.
Imagine a quiet garden after rain. The smell of wet earth. Drops falling from a leaf.
Let the image go and rest in the stillness that remains.
Repeat your intention three more times, and let it settle.
Feel the breath growing a little deeper, a little fuller.
Notice the floor beneath you and the sounds of the room.
Move gently, stretch if you like, and roll to one side before you sit up.

meditations.title: Full Body Scan
meditations.subtitle: Head-to-toe awareness
meditations.about: A precise, awake scan from the crown of the head to the soles of the feet. It trains steady attention and leaves the body deeply rested.

script.text: Lie down or sit comfortably with your eyes closed. Let the body be still.
We will move attention slowly from the crown of the head to the feet, simply feeling whatever is there.
Start at the very top of the head. Notice any tingling, warmth, or nothing at all. All of it is fine.
The forehead and temples. Let any frown dissolve.
The eyes and the small muscles around them. The cheeks. The nose and the breath moving through it.
The mouth, the jaw, the tongue. Let the teeth part slightly.
The throat and the back of the neck. Let them be soft.
The shoulders, then the upper arms, elbows, forearms, wrists, hands and each finger.
The chest and upper back. Feel them move as you breathe.
The belly and lower back. Notice the gentle rise and fall.
The pelvis and hips. Heavy and grounded.
The thighs, the knees, the calves, the ankles.
The tops of the feet, the soles, each toe.
Now sense the whole body breathing, as one complete field of sensation.
Stay with that wide awareness, steady and calm.
When the mind wanders, return to the whole body breathing.
Rest here, awake and at ease.
Gently deepen the breath and begin to move your fingers and toes.
Open your eyes when you are ready.

meditations.title: 61-Point Relaxation
meditations.subtitle: A classical journey of light points
meditations.about: Inspired by the classical Himalayan practice of shavayatra, attention travels through a sequence of points, picturing a small star of light at each. It is precise, absorbing and deeply restful.

script.text: Lie on your back in Savasana, the body straight, arms a little away, palms up. Close your eyes.
We will travel through a series of points in the body. At each one, picture a tiny, soft star of light, and then move on.
Begin at the point between the eyebrows. Picture a small star of light there.
Move to the hollow of the throat. Then the right shoulder, the right elbow, the right wrist.
The tip of the right thumb, then each fingertip in turn: index, middle, ring and little finger.
Back to the right wrist, the right elbow, the right shoulder, and the hollow of the throat.
The left shoulder, the left elbow, the left wrist. The left thumb and each fingertip in turn.
Back to the left wrist, the left elbow, the left shoulder, and the hollow of the throat.
The centre of the chest. The right side of the chest. The centre. The left side of the chest. The centre again.
The navel. The centre of the pelvis. The right hip, the right knee, the right ankle, the tip of the right big toe and each toe in turn.
Back up to the right ankle, the right knee, the right hip, and the centre of the pelvis.
The left hip, the left knee, the left ankle, the tip of the left big toe and each toe in turn.
Back up to the left ankle, the left knee, the left hip, the pelvis, the navel, the centre of the chest, the throat, and the point between the eyebrows.
Now picture all the stars at once, the whole body outlined in soft, quiet light.
Rest in that picture. Nothing to do. Simply aware.
If the points blur, that is fine. Let the whole body glow and rest.
Let the stars fade, and feel the body lying heavy on the floor.
Breathe a little deeper, stretch, and roll to your side before you sit up.

meditations.title: Starlight Yoga Nidra
meditations.subtitle: A long yogic sleep under the night sky
meditations.about: The full Yoga Nidra journey with extra time for breath, opposite sensations and night-sky imagery. Use it for deep rest, or at bedtime and simply let sleep take over.

script.text: Welcome. Lie down on your back, cover yourself with a blanket if you like, and let the eyes close.
Settle completely. In this practice the body sleeps, while a small part of you keeps listening.
Listen for the farthest sound you can hear. Then a nearer sound. Then the sound of your own breath.
Feel the body lying on the floor, and say silently to yourself: I am practising Yoga Nidra. I am awake and relaxed.
Now bring a sankalpa to mind, a simple positive intention. Repeat it three times, clearly and sincerely.
Right side. Right hand thumb, each finger, palm, back of the hand, wrist, elbow, shoulder, armpit, waist, hip, thigh, knee, calf, ankle, heel, sole, and each toe.
Left side. Left hand thumb, each finger, palm, back of the hand, wrist, elbow, shoulder, armpit, waist, hip, thigh, knee, calf, ankle, heel, sole, and each toe.
Back of the body. Both heels, calves, thighs, buttocks, lower back, middle back, upper back, shoulder blades, the back of the neck, the back of the head.
Front of the body. Crown, forehead, both eyebrows, the space between them, eyelids, eyes, nose, cheeks, lips, jaw, chin, throat, chest, navel, belly, pelvis.
Major parts. The whole right leg. The whole left leg. Both legs together. The whole right arm, the left arm, both arms. The whole back. The whole front. The whole body.
Become aware of the breath at the navel. The belly rises as you breathe in, falls as you breathe out.
Move awareness to the chest. Feel the breath gently moving the ribs.
Now feel the breath in the throat, cool on the way in, warm on the way out.
Count backward, one number for each full breath, from thirty-three down to one. If you lose the count, start again from thirty-three.
Let the counting go. Experience heaviness. The body is so heavy it sinks into the ground.
Experience lightness. The body is so light it floats up like a leaf on a warm wind.
Experience cold, like walking barefoot on a winter night. Then heat, like resting in summer sun.
Let the sensations go. Now picture the night sky at its very darkest.
One by one, stars appear. A few, then hundreds, then a whole river of light across the sky.
Picture the moon rising slowly over a quiet sea, silver light spreading across the water.
Picture a single lamp in a small window, far away, warm and steady.
Let all the images go. Rest in the dark, open space behind the eyes.
Remember your sankalpa now. Repeat it three times, exactly as before.
Become aware of the breath once more, deep and slow.
If you are going to sleep, stay here and let sleep come. If not, begin to feel the floor and the room around you.
Move slowly, stretch, and roll to your right side before sitting up. Yoga Nidra is complete.

meditations.title: Muladhara · Root
meditations.subtitle: Grounded, steady, safe
meditations.about: In yoga's traditional map, Muladhara sits at the base of the spine and is linked with the earth element. This sitting focuses on stability, support and the feeling of being held.

script.text: Sit comfortably on the floor, a cushion or a chair, with both sit bones heavy and the spine tall. Close your eyes.
Today we rest attention on Muladhara, the root, at the base of the spine. In the old texts its element is earth.
Feel every place your body touches the ground. The sit bones, the legs, the feet.
Breathe out slowly and let the weight sink down, as if roots were growing from the base of the spine into the earth.
Picture rich red earth beneath you, warm and steady.
Breathing in, I am supported. Breathing out, I am steady.
The traditional seed sound of the root is Lam. If you like, hum it softly on the exhale, or just hear it inwardly.
Lam. Feel the sound settle low in the body.
Notice anything you are holding tightly, in the belly, the jaw, or the hands. Let it rest on the ground too.
Feel how the earth simply holds you, without effort, without conditions.
Stay with the heavy, safe feeling at the base of the spine.
Let the sound fade, and keep that rooted feeling as you open your eyes.
Stand up slowly and feel your feet on the floor.

meditations.title: Svadhisthana · Sacral
meditations.subtitle: Flow like water
meditations.about: Svadhisthana, below the navel, is linked with the water element in yoga's traditional map. This meditation invites ease, movement and a softer relationship with feeling.

script.text: Sit comfortably, or lie down with the knees bent. Rest your hands just below the navel.
We turn to Svadhisthana, the sacral centre. Its traditional element is water.
Breathe into the space beneath your hands. Feel the belly gently fill and empty.
Let the hips and pelvis soften, as if they were floating.
Picture a calm lake at sunset, warm orange light moving across the water.
If you like, let the body sway a little from side to side, slow as a ripple, then become still again.
Notice what you are feeling right now. Let it move through you, the way water moves, without being held.
The traditional seed sound here is Vam. Hum it softly on the out-breath, or simply listen inwardly.
Vam. Feel the sound ripple through the lower belly.
Let pleasure be simple: the warmth of your hands, the ease of a breath.
Rest in the flowing feeling, soft and unhurried.
Let the water grow still and clear.
Take a deep breath, and gently open your eyes.

meditations.title: Manipura · Solar Plexus
meditations.subtitle: Kindle quiet confidence
meditations.about: Manipura, the jewel city at the navel, is associated with the fire element. This bright, upright sitting builds a calm, steady sense of will and warmth.

script.text: Sit tall with a long spine and open shoulders. Rest the hands on the knees, palms up.
We bring attention to Manipura, at the navel and solar plexus. In yoga's traditional map, its element is fire.
Breathe in and feel the belly expand. Breathe out and feel the navel draw softly toward the spine.
Picture a small golden sun glowing just above the navel.
With each in-breath, the sun grows a little warmer and brighter.
Feel the strength of your spine, upright without strain.
Bring to mind one thing you want to do with steady effort. Not with force, but with warmth.
Say silently: I can take the next step.
The traditional seed sound of this centre is Ram. Hum it on the exhale, or hear it inwardly.
Ram. Let the sound glow at the centre of the body.
Rest in the steady warmth. Bright, but calm.
Let the sun settle into a quiet, steady glow.
Open your eyes and carry that warmth into your day.

meditations.title: Anahata · Heart
meditations.subtitle: Open, unhurried kindness
meditations.about: Anahata, the unstruck sound, sits at the centre of the chest and is linked with the air element. This sitting softens the chest and grows warmth for yourself and others.

script.text: Sit comfortably and rest one or both hands over the centre of your chest.
We turn to Anahata, the heart centre. Its traditional element is air, open and spacious.
Feel the breath move under your hands. The chest rising, and falling.
Let the shoulders drop and the upper back widen, as if the heart had a little more room.
Picture fresh green leaves in morning light, open to the sky.
Bring to mind someone who makes you smile. Notice the warmth that appears.
Silently offer them a wish: may you be happy. May you be well.
Now turn the same wish toward yourself: may I be happy. May I be well.
Let the warmth spread out, to people you pass each day, and then wider still.
The traditional seed sound of the heart is Yam. Hum it softly, or hear it inwardly.
Yam. Feel the sound open across the chest.
Breathe in kindness. Breathe out kindness.
Rest in the open, quiet space of the heart.
Keep your hands on your chest for one more breath.
Gently open your eyes, and carry this kindness with you.

meditations.title: Vishuddha · Throat
meditations.subtitle: Space to speak and listen
meditations.about: Vishuddha, the purifier, sits at the throat and is linked with space in yoga's traditional map. This practice softens the neck and jaw and invites honest, gentle expression.

script.text: Sit tall, with the chin level and the back of the neck long. Let the eyes close.
We turn to Vishuddha, at the throat. In the old texts, its element is space.
Slowly turn the head right, back to centre, then left, and back to centre. Let the neck be easy.
Unclench the jaw. Let the tongue rest on the floor of the mouth.
Picture a wide, clear blue sky above a calm sea. Endless room.
Feel the breath passing through the throat. Cool as it enters, warm as it leaves.
Is there something you have wanted to say? Let it be heard, kindly, here in silence.
Now listen. Notice the sounds around you, and the quiet beneath them.
The traditional seed sound here is Ham. Hum it on the out-breath, feeling the vibration in the throat.
Ham. Let the sound be easy and unforced.
Rest in the open space of the throat, ready to speak, ready to listen.
Let the sound fade into silence.
Swallow, soften the jaw, and slowly open your eyes.

meditations.title: Ajna · Third Eye
meditations.subtitle: Clear, steady attention
meditations.about: Ajna, the command centre, sits between the eyebrows. Classical practices use it as a point of concentration, and this sitting trains calm, clear focus there.

script.text: Sit tall and still, hands resting on the knees, and close your eyes.
We bring attention to Ajna, the point between the eyebrows, used in many yoga traditions as a seat for concentration.
Let the eyes relax completely. You do not need to look upward. Simply feel the space between the eyebrows.
Notice any sensation there: warmth, pressure, tingling, or simply space.
Picture a deep twilight sky, and one small star appearing in the middle of it.
Rest your attention on that star. When thoughts arrive, let them pass behind it like clouds.
Each time you return to the star, you are training attention. That return is the practice.
Breathe softly, as if the breath itself flowed in and out through the point between the brows.
The traditional sound of this centre is Om. Hum it once on the out-breath, or hear it inwardly.
Om. Then listen to the silence that follows.
Notice the one who is watching. Calm, clear, unmoved.
Stay with the star, the silence and the steady watching.
Let the attention grow lighter, without losing it.
Let the star fade, and widen your attention to the whole body.
Slowly open your eyes and look around the room.

meditations.title: Sahasrara · Crown
meditations.subtitle: Rest in open awareness
meditations.about: Sahasrara, the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown, is described as beyond the elements. This quiet sitting rests in wide, open awareness.

script.text: Sit comfortably with the spine tall, as if a thread drew you gently up through the crown of the head.
We rest attention at Sahasrara, the crown, pictured in the old texts as a lotus of a thousand petals.
Feel the very top of the head. Let the scalp soften.
Picture soft light resting on the crown, like dawn touching the top of a high mountain.
With each breath, the light opens a little more, petal by petal.
Let the light flow down slowly through the face, the throat, the heart, the belly, to the base of the spine.
Now feel the whole body lit from within, quiet and steady.
Let go of doing anything at all. Simply be aware of being aware.
Sounds come and go. Thoughts come and go. Awareness stays.
Rest like the sky, which holds every cloud and is never stained by them.
If you like, silently repeat: I am here.
Then let even those words dissolve into silence.
Stay in the silence, open and at ease.
Nothing to reach for. Nothing to push away.
Feel the body sitting here, and the breath moving through it.
Bring your palms together at the heart, and slowly open your eyes.

meditations.title: Seven Chakra Journey
meditations.subtitle: Root to crown in one sitting
meditations.about: A complete journey through yoga's traditional map of seven centres, with each one's seed sound and image. Think of it as a structured way to move attention up the spine, from stability to stillness.

script.text: Sit tall and comfortable, or lie down if you prefer. Close your eyes and take three slow breaths.
We will travel up the spine through the seven chakras, the traditional centres of attention in yoga, from the root to the crown.
Muladhara, the root, at the base of the spine. Feel the ground beneath you, steady as warm red earth.
Its seed sound is Lam. Hum it once, or hear it inwardly, and feel solid support.
Svadhisthana, the sacral centre, below the navel. Picture warm orange light moving on calm water.
Its seed sound is Vam. Let the hips soften and the breath flow freely.
Manipura, at the navel. Picture a small golden sun, warm and bright.
Its seed sound is Ram. Feel a calm, steady strength in the centre of the body.
Anahata, at the centre of the chest. Picture fresh green leaves opening to the light.
Its seed sound is Yam. Let kindness widen across the chest, for yourself and others.
Vishuddha, at the throat. Picture a wide, clear blue sky.
Its seed sound is Ham. Let the jaw soften and the throat feel open and easy.
Ajna, between the eyebrows. Picture deep twilight, and one steady star.
Its sound is Om. Let attention gather there, clear and calm.
Sahasrara, at the crown of the head. Picture soft light, opening like a lotus of a thousand petals.
Here there is no sound, only silence. Rest in it.
Now feel all seven centres at once, a column of soft light from the base of the spine to the crown.
Breathe up the spine from root to crown, and down again from crown to root.
Let the breath go, and simply rest, steady below and open above.
Stay in this balanced stillness for a few more breaths.
Let the attention return slowly to the heart, the centre between above and below.
Feel the whole body, the breath, and the ground holding you.
Bring your palms together, take a full breath, and gently open your eyes.

meditations.title: Box Breathing
meditations.subtitle: A steady 4-count rhythm; skip holds anytime
meditations.about: Four equal sides: breathe in, pause, breathe out, pause. A simple, structured rhythm that many people use to settle before a busy moment.

script.text: Sit tall and comfortable, and let your shoulders drop.
Follow the circle: in for four, pause for four, out for four, pause for four.
Breathe in quietly through the nose, filling from the belly upward.
In the pause, stay soft. There is no need to grip the throat.
Let the out-breath be smooth and unhurried, all the way to the end.
If the holds feel uncomfortable, skip them and just breathe in and out with the circle.
Picture tracing the four sides of a square as you breathe.
If you feel light-headed or uneasy at any point, let the technique go and simply breathe naturally.
Let the breath return to its own rhythm.
Notice how steady you feel now.

meditations.title: 4-7-8 Relaxing Breath
meditations.subtitle: A long exhale; skip the hold anytime
meditations.about: Breathe in for four, rest for seven, and breathe out for eight. A long, slow exhale is a gentle way to downshift at the end of the day.

script.text: Sit or lie comfortably, and rest the tip of the tongue just behind the upper front teeth.
Follow the circle: in for four, rest for seven, out for eight.
Breathe in quietly through the nose.
In the pause, let the body be still and the shoulders soft.
Breathe out slowly through the mouth, as if sighing through a straw.
If seven counts feels long, shorten the pause or skip it entirely. The long exhale matters most.
With each out-breath, let the body sink a little deeper.
Notice the moment of stillness at the end of each exhale.
If you feel light-headed or uneasy at any point, let the technique go and simply breathe naturally.
Let the counting go and breathe naturally.
Rest here for a moment before you move on.

meditations.title: Breath of Energy
meditations.subtitle: Wake up in five minutes
meditations.about: An even, upright breathing rhythm with simple posture cues to wake up the body. Gentle enough for any morning.

script.text: Sit or stand tall, with the chest lifted and the shoulders easy.
Follow the circle with full, even breaths: four in, four out.
Breathe in and feel the ribs widen to the sides.
Breathe out and feel the navel draw gently in.
Lift the crown of the head a little higher with each in-breath.
Let the eyes stay open and soft, taking in the light around you.
Feel warmth building in the body, steady and alert.
Keep the breath smooth. Full, but never forced.
Take one last full breath in, and let it go with a sigh.
Notice your energy, and step into the day.

meditations.title: Ujjayi: Ocean Breath
meditations.subtitle: The breath of flowing yoga
meditations.about: Ujjayi, the victorious breath, gently narrows the throat to create a soft ocean sound. It is the breath of Ashtanga and vinyasa practice.

script.text: Sit tall and close the mouth. Breathe in and out through the nose.
We will add a gentle narrowing at the back of the throat, making a soft sound like distant waves.
First, breathe out through an open mouth as if fogging a mirror: haaa. Feel the throat narrow slightly.
Now close the mouth and keep that same gentle narrowing as you breathe out through the nose.
Try it on the in-breath too. A soft, even sound, like the sea heard from far away.
Keep the sound soft, just loud enough for you to hear, and never strain.
Follow the circle: five counts in, six counts out.
Let the sound become a steady rhythm to rest your attention on.
If the throat feels tight or tired, release the sound and breathe normally.
Listen. Waves coming in, waves going out.
Let the sound fade and return to a natural breath.
Notice the calm, steady feeling it leaves behind.

meditations.title: Nadi Shodhana
meditations.subtitle: Alternate-nostril balance
meditations.about: Nadi Shodhana, channel cleansing, alternates the breath between the nostrils. It is one of the most widely taught pranayama practices for a calm, balanced mind.

script.text: Sit tall and rest the left hand on the knee. Lift the right hand to the face.
Fold the index and middle fingers toward the palm. The thumb will close the right nostril, the ring finger the left.
Close the right nostril with the thumb. Breathe in slowly through the left.
Close the left with the ring finger, release the thumb, and breathe out through the right.
Breathe in through the right. Close it, release the left, and breathe out through the left. That is one round.
Continue at your own pace, following the circle: four in, six out. Keep the touch of the fingers light.
If the arm tires, rest it for a few breaths, and simply picture the breath alternating.
Picture two rivers meeting and flowing on as one, calm and wide.
Let the breath be silent and smooth, never forced.
In through the left, out through the right. In through the right, out through the left.
If you feel light-headed or uneasy at any point, let the technique go and simply breathe naturally.
Finish by breathing out through the left nostril, then rest the hand on the knee.
Breathe naturally through both nostrils, and notice the quiet that remains.

meditations.title: Chandra Bhedana: Moon Breath
meditations.subtitle: A cooling left-nostril rhythm
meditations.about: In yoga tradition the left nostril is linked with the moon and a cooler, quieter quality. This evening practice breathes in through the left and out through the right.

script.text: Sit comfortably, spine tall. Rest the left hand on the knee and bring the right hand to the face.
Fold the index and middle fingers in. The thumb closes the right nostril, the ring finger the left.
Close the right nostril with the thumb and breathe in gently through the left.
Close the left with the ring finger, release the thumb, and breathe out slowly through the right.
Return to the start: close the right, breathe in through the left. Out through the right.
Follow the circle: four counts in, six counts out. Let the out-breath be the longer one.
Picture moonlight on still water, cool and silver.
Keep the face soft and the shoulders low.
If you feel light-headed or uneasy at any point, let the technique go and simply breathe naturally.
Release the hand, and breathe naturally through both nostrils.
Notice the cool, quiet feeling, and carry it into your evening.

meditations.title: Bhramari: Bee Breath
meditations.subtitle: Humming the mind quiet
meditations.about: Bhramari is named after the humming black bee. A soft, steady hum on a long exhale is one of the simplest ways yoga offers to quiet a busy mind.

script.text: Sit comfortably with the spine tall and the face relaxed. Close your eyes.
We will breathe in through the nose, and breathe out with a soft humming sound, like a bee.
Breathe in quietly through the nose. Then, with the lips closed and the teeth slightly apart, hum on the out-breath: mmmm.
Let the hum be low and easy. Feel it vibrate in the lips, the face and the skull.
If you like, gently press the small flaps at the front of the ears closed with your index fingers.
Follow the circle: four counts in, then a long, humming out-breath.
Between rounds, pause and listen to the silence inside.
Keep the hum comfortable. Softer is fine. You can also hum silently.
Feel the sound washing through the head, smoothing the edges of thought.
Release the hands and let the last hum fade.
Sit for a few breaths in the quiet it leaves behind.

meditations.title: Sitali: Cooling Breath
meditations.subtitle: Cool down when you feel heated
meditations.about: Sitali draws the breath in over a curled tongue so it feels cool, then lets it out through the nose. If your tongue does not curl, Sitkari, breathing through lightly closed teeth, works just as well.

script.text: Sit tall and relaxed, hands resting on the knees.
We will breathe in through the mouth so the air feels cool, and breathe out through the nose.
Curl the sides of the tongue into a tube, and let the tip rest just past the lips. Breathe in slowly through the tube.
If your tongue does not curl, part the lips, keep the teeth lightly together, and breathe in through the teeth instead.
Close the mouth and breathe out slowly through the nose.
Follow the circle: four in through the mouth, six out through the nose.
Feel the cool air on the tongue and the warmer air leaving through the nose.
Picture morning dew on fresh green leaves.
If you feel light-headed or uneasy at any point, let the technique go and simply breathe naturally.
Close the mouth and return to natural breathing.
Notice the cool, clear feeling across the face and body.

meditations.title: Ocean Calm
meditations.subtitle: Breathe with the waves
meditations.about: Ride the rhythm of the waves to slow everything down. A gentle reset for any time the day feels too fast.

script.text: Sit or lie comfortably, and let your eyes close or soften.
Listen to the waves for a moment. There is nothing you need to do.
Breathe in as a wave rolls in. Breathe out as it slides back to the sea.
Let your out-breath be a little longer than your in-breath.
Notice where the body is holding tension: the forehead, the jaw, the shoulders, the hands.
With the next wave going out, let one of those places soften.
Picture standing at the edge of the sea, the water washing over your feet, and drawing back.
Each wave takes a little of the rush of the day with it.
If thoughts keep arriving, let them be waves too. They rise, they fall, they leave.
Your breath can be as steady as the tide.
Feel the ground beneath you, solid like the shore.
Soft belly. Soft shoulders. Soft face.
You are calmer than you were a few minutes ago.
Take one more deep breath with the waves.
When you are ready, open your eyes and carry this calm with you.

meditations.title: Soften & Release
meditations.subtitle: Let tension melt away
meditations.about: A short tense-and-release practice that helps the body let go of stress you might not even notice you are carrying.

script.text: Sit or lie comfortably and close your eyes.
We will gently tense and release parts of the body, so you can feel the difference between holding and letting go.
Make two soft fists and squeeze for three breaths. Now let the hands fall open.
Lift the shoulders toward the ears, hold, and let them drop with a sigh.
Scrunch the face, eyes and nose, then let everything soften and spread.
Press the feet into the floor, tense the legs, and let them go heavy.
Draw the belly in, hold, and let it become completely soft.
Now scan the whole body. Wherever you find holding, breathe out and let it melt like warm wax.
Breathe in calm. Breathe out tension.
Notice how much lighter the body feels.
Rest in the softness.
Take a full breath in, and let it out slowly.
Open your eyes when you are ready.

meditations.title: Rain on the Roof
meditations.subtitle: Stillness in soft rain
meditations.about: Use the sound of steady rain as an anchor for attention. A cosy, quiet practice for an overloaded mind.

script.text: Get comfortable, perhaps with a blanket, and close your eyes.
Listen to the rain. Let it be the only thing you need to pay attention to.
Notice the many sounds inside the rain: heavy drops, soft drops, a steady hush underneath.
Picture sitting by a window, warm and dry, watching rain run down the glass.
Let each drop be a thought, landing, sliding, and running away.
There is no need to stop the thoughts. Just watch them fall.
Breathe slowly. In, and out.
Feel the warmth of your body, safe and sheltered.
When you notice you have drifted into thinking, come back to the sound of the rain.
Let the rain wash the edges of the day.
Soften the shoulders. Soften the belly.
Listen to the spaces between the drops.
Rest in the sound, held and calm.
Let the breath slow to the pace of the rain.
Keep listening for a few breaths more.
Gently open your eyes, rested and clear.

meditations.title: Metta: Loving-Kindness
meditations.subtitle: Warmth for yourself and others
meditations.about: A classic practice of offering kind wishes, first to yourself, then to others, then to everyone. Simple phrases that grow a warmer, steadier heart.

script.text: Sit comfortably and rest one hand over your heart.
We will offer kind wishes, starting with ourselves, and moving gently outward.
Silently say: may I be safe. May I be well. May I be at ease.
Feel the warmth of your hand and the rise of your chest as you repeat the words.
Bring to mind someone you love easily. Picture their face. May you be safe. May you be well. May you be at ease.
Now someone neutral, perhaps a person you passed today. May you be happy. May you be at ease.
Now someone you find difficult, only as much as feels possible. May you be well.
If that is hard, return to yourself for a moment. May I be kind to myself.
Now let the wish spread to everyone in this building, this town, this country.
May all beings be safe. May all beings be well. May all beings be at peace.
Rest in the warmth that remains.
Breathe in kindness, breathe out kindness.
Let the words go, and keep the feeling.
Return to yourself once more. May I be kind to myself today.
Gently open your eyes, and carry that warmth with you.

meditations.title: Morning Clarity
meditations.subtitle: Greet the day with intention
meditations.about: A short, bright sitting to wake up the body, clear the mind and choose how you want the day to feel.

script.text: Good morning. Sit up tall and take a moment to arrive.
This is your time, before the day begins.
Take a deep breath in and feel the body widen. Breathe out any heaviness from sleep.
Roll the shoulders back once or twice, and lift the crown of the head.
Picture golden morning light on your face.
Notice the sounds of the morning around you.
Think of one thing you are looking forward to today, however small.
Now choose one word for how you want to feel today: calm, steady, open, kind.
Breathe that word in. Let it fill the whole body.
You have everything you need for today.
Take one last full breath.
Open your eyes and step into your day with clarity.

meditations.title: Gratitude Sunrise
meditations.subtitle: Begin with a full heart
meditations.about: Start the day by noticing what is already good. Santosha, contentment, is one of yoga's classic niyamas.

script.text: Sit comfortably, close your eyes, and breathe a few slow breaths.
In yoga, santosha means contentment. We will start the day by noticing what is already here.
Notice something simple your body did for you today: waking, breathing, standing up.
Silently say thank you to it.
Bring to mind a person you are grateful for. Picture them clearly. Let the feeling grow.
Notice something in your home or your surroundings you are glad to have.
Remember a small moment from yesterday that made you smile.
Let the gratitude rest in the chest like warm morning sun.
Notice that nothing needs to change for this moment to be enough.
Breathe in thanks. Breathe out ease.
Choose one way to share a little kindness today.
Rest in the warmth for a few more breaths.
Carry this full heart into your morning.
Open your eyes and begin.

meditations.title: Sankalpa: Set Your Intention
meditations.subtitle: A heartfelt resolve for the day
meditations.about: A sankalpa is a short, sincere resolve, stated as if it were already true. This morning practice helps you find one and plant it.

script.text: Sit comfortably, spine tall, and let the eyes close.
A sankalpa is a short, heartfelt resolve. Today we will find one and plant it like a seed.
Take a few slow breaths and let the body settle.
Ask quietly: what matters most to me right now?
Let an answer arise, without forcing it. It may be a word, an image or a feeling.
Shape it into a short sentence in the present tense, as if it were already true. For example: I am patient. I meet the day with courage.
Repeat your sankalpa silently three times, slowly and sincerely.
Feel where it lands in the body. Perhaps the chest, perhaps the belly.
Picture a small flame of a lamp, steady and warm. Your sankalpa rests in that light.
Let it go now, trusting it is planted.
Repeat your sankalpa one last time.
Open your eyes and let it guide your day.

meditations.title: Trataka: Steady Gaze
meditations.subtitle: Candle gazing for a settled mind
meditations.about: Trataka is the classical practice of steady gazing, traditionally at a candle flame. Without a candle, gaze softly at a small dot or object instead.

script.text: Place a candle at arm's length, level with your eyes, in a room without drafts. Or choose a small dot or object to look at.
Sit tall and comfortable. Never leave a candle unattended, and close the eyes whenever they need a rest.
Look softly at the flame, or your point. Keep the eyes relaxed, blinking whenever you need to.
Let the gaze rest at the brightest part of the flame, just above the wick.
Notice how the mind settles as the eyes become still.
When the eyes feel tired or watery, close them.
With the eyes closed, notice the after-image of the flame in front of you. Watch it gently until it fades.
Open the eyes and gaze again, softly and steadily.
Thoughts may arrive. Let them pass around the flame and return to looking.
Close the eyes again and watch the inner image, still and quiet.
Let the inner image fade into a calm, dark space.
Rest in that dark, steady stillness.
If you like, one last time, open the eyes, gaze briefly, and close them again.
Cup the palms over the eyes for a few breaths, then lower the hands.
Open your eyes slowly. Remember to put out the candle.

meditations.title: Singing Bowl Focus
meditations.subtitle: Ride the sound into stillness
meditations.about: Use the rising and fading tones of singing bowls as a point of focus. Each tone becomes a doorway into the silence after it.

script.text: Sit tall and comfortable, and close your eyes.
We will let the sound of the bowls be the anchor for attention.
Listen to one tone from the moment it begins until it disappears completely.
Notice the exact moment the sound becomes silence.
When the next tone rises, follow it again, beginning to end.
If the mind wanders, the next tone is always there to bring you back.
Notice how the sound is not only in the ears, but in the chest and the face too.
Let the breath slow down to match the long, fading tones.
Rest in the silence between sounds. It is just as important as the sound.
Attention gathers like ripples settling on water.
Notice the calm, clear quality of the mind right now.
Keep listening, each tone a new beginning.
Let the listening become effortless.
Let the mind rest here, clear and calm.
Slowly widen your attention to the room around you.
Carry this clarity into your next task.

meditations.title: Om: Sound Meditation
meditations.subtitle: Feel the vibration of sound
meditations.about: Om, also written Aum, is the best known sound in yoga. The Mandukya Upanishad describes its parts, A, U, M and the silence after, as states of awareness.

script.text: Sit tall, close your eyes, and rest the hands on the knees.
We will chant Om, aloud or silently, and rest in the silence that follows each one.
Breathe in deeply. On the out-breath, let the sound flow: Aaa, Ooo, Mmm.
Feel Aaa open in the belly, Ooo rise through the chest, and Mmm hum in the head.
Notice the silence after the sound. In the old teaching, this silence is the fourth part of Om.
Breathe in again, and chant once more, a little softer.
If you prefer, simply hum, or hear the sound in your mind.
Let each Om carry away a little restlessness.
Chant a few more rounds at your own pace, resting in silence between them.
Now let the sound go completely, and rest in the quiet.
Notice the stillness that the sound has left behind.
Let the last vibration fade, and listen to the quiet.
Gently open your eyes.

meditations.title: So Hum: Breath Mantra
meditations.subtitle: The mantra that is already breathing
meditations.about: So Hum, often translated as I am that, is a classic mantra that links silently with the breath. It is easy to learn and easy to return to anywhere.

script.text: Sit comfortably and close your eyes. Let the breath find its own pace.
We will pair the breath with a simple mantra: so on the in-breath, hum on the out-breath.
As you breathe in, silently hear the sound so.
As you breathe out, silently hear the sound hum.
Do not change the breath to fit the words. Let the words ride on the breath.
So, as the breath flows in. Hum, as it flows out.
When the mind wanders, notice where it went, and come back to the next so.
Let the mantra become softer, almost a whisper in the mind.
Notice the tiny pause at the top and the bottom of each breath.
If the words fade on their own, rest in the quiet breathing.
When you notice you are thinking again, gently return to so, and hum.
Let the practice become effortless, like a song you know by heart.
Rest in the quiet beneath the mantra.
Let the mantra go, and sit quietly for a few breaths.
Slowly open your eyes.

meditations.title: Antar Mouna: Inner Silence
meditations.subtitle: Watch the mind, without getting lost
meditations.about: Inspired by the classical practice of antar mouna, inner silence, you move from listening to the outside world to calmly watching your own thoughts. It builds the steady witness at the heart of meditation.

script.text: Sit comfortably, spine tall, and close your eyes.
We begin with the outside world and slowly turn inward, like mist settling on a still lake.
Listen to the sounds around you. Name them silently if you like: traffic, wind, voices, breath.
Let your attention move from one sound to another, without staying with any of them.
Now notice the body sitting here. The weight, the warmth, the breath.
Now turn toward the mind. Watch what thoughts arise, as if you were sitting on the bank of a river.
Do not follow the thoughts and do not push them away. Simply notice: a thought is here.
Notice whether thoughts are pictures, words or feelings.
If you get carried away by a thought, that is normal. Step back onto the bank.
Notice the space between one thought and the next.
Rest in that space for a moment, however brief.
You are the one who watches. Thoughts come and go. The watcher stays.
Let the mind grow quiet on its own, like a lake when the wind drops.
Rest in the stillness.
Slowly become aware of the body and the sounds around you again.
Gently open your eyes.

achievements.title: Journey Complete
achievements.description: Finish every day of a plan

dailyChallenges.title: A moment in Mountain
dailyChallenges.description: Stand with feet grounded and notice three easy breaths.

dailyChallenges.title: Unroll your mat
dailyChallenges.description: Set out your mat and spend one minute sitting or standing on it.

dailyChallenges.title: Chair Cat and Cow
dailyChallenges.description: Sit on a steady chair and gently round and lengthen your back five times.

dailyChallenges.title: Try a supported Tree
dailyChallenges.description: Keep one hand on a wall and your lifted toes on the floor for three breaths per side.

dailyChallenges.title: A morning reach
dailyChallenges.description: Reach your arms up with an inhale, then lower them as you exhale. Repeat three times.

dailyChallenges.title: Make room for rest
dailyChallenges.description: Lie down with a cushion beneath your knees for one quiet minute.

dailyChallenges.title: Notice your breath
dailyChallenges.description: Pause before practice and observe five breaths without changing them.

dailyChallenges.title: Prepare a prop
dailyChallenges.description: Place a folded blanket beside your mat for your next practice.

dailyChallenges.title: Soften your fold
dailyChallenges.description: Try a standing fold with bent knees and hands supported on a steady chair.

dailyChallenges.title: Practice without a screen
dailyChallenges.description: Put your phone aside and explore one familiar pose for a minute.

dailyChallenges.title: Choose tomorrow’s moment
dailyChallenges.description: Pick a realistic time for tomorrow’s yoga and leave yourself a reminder.

dailyChallenges.title: An evening pause
dailyChallenges.description: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest for five unhurried breaths.

dailyChallenges.title: Set a kind intention
dailyChallenges.description: Before yoga, choose one word to guide your practice today.

dailyChallenges.title: Walk into your practice
dailyChallenges.description: Take five slow steps toward your mat, noticing each foot meeting the floor.

dailyChallenges.title: Sip and settle
dailyChallenges.description: Have some water nearby, then take a comfortable seat before practice.

dailyChallenges.title: Try a quiet practice
dailyChallenges.description: Turn off background music for a minute and listen to your natural breathing.

dailyChallenges.title: Soften your expression
dailyChallenges.description: During one familiar pose, release your jaw and notice your brow.

dailyChallenges.title: A pause before coffee
dailyChallenges.description: Before your usual morning drink, sit tall for three natural breaths.

dailyChallenges.title: Notice your effort
dailyChallenges.description: After practice, name one choice that helped you listen to your body.

dailyChallenges.title: One gentle sun greeting
dailyChallenges.description: Try one slow, familiar sun greeting, pausing whenever you need another breath.

quotes.text: Yoga is the cessation of movements in the consciousness.

quotes.text: Asana is perfect firmness of body, steadiness of intelligence and benevolence of spirit.
quotes.author: Patanjali — Yoga Sutras 2.46, translated by B.K.S. Iyengar

quotes.text: Yoga is a light, which once lit will never dim.
quotes.author: B.K.S. Iyengar

quotes.text: The body is your temple. Keep it pure and clean for the soul to reside in.
quotes.author: B.K.S. Iyengar

quotes.text: It is through your body that you realize you are a spark of divinity.
quotes.author: B.K.S. Iyengar

quotes.text: The present moment is filled with joy and happiness. If you are attentive, you will see it.
